vinruviel.name: Vinruviel
vinruviel.species: Entity (Possibly Cosmic Being) created by itself, without the intervention of the One Above All
vinruviel.origin: ===Origin=== thumb|left|Mother Vinruviel The One Above All created Earth and the Demiurge Primordial, who seeded Earth with life, all according to the One Above All's design. The first of those creatures were the Elder Gods, who shaped Earth according to His design. Vinruviel, the Mother of Horrors was an entity that came to be from itself and not from the One Above All. The Mother of Horrors resented the One Above All for dominating over all of existence, and decided that the planet Earth, to which she was bound to, would not know His rule, only hers and that of her children. She hid Earth from the One Above All, and began filling it with her creation. ===Early years=== ====The Seed of Corruption==== With her coming, life began to change. She planted seeds of shadow within the sleeping Elder Gods. As the Mother's corruption changed the creatures of Earth, the Elder Gods grew into fearsome and hungry creatures, many of them eventually becoming demons. Gaea was one of the few creatures uncorrupted, and she loved the Volantine Choir, a race of winged creatures living atop great sunlit forests. Vinruviel came to the Volantine, corrupting them, allowing them to also be diggers, and them leading to ravage their forests to built tunnels, burrows, and the first city on Earth. She also blessed with great size and strength one of them, whom she named Gologolthia ("keeper of my children"). She created her oldest child. ====The Great Culling==== The One Above All came to notice that His creation had been corrupted. This is also attributed to Gaea who feared all life would be wiped out on Earth, as the Elder Gods' constant fighting prevented even her hardiest creations survived during the Godwar-. Either on Gaea's plea to the Demiurge, or on the One Above All's decision, Gaea and Demiurge produced the Demogorge, born as Atum. Wielding the powers of the Sun, Atum decimated the demons, absorbing their forms and energies. Eventually, Atum transformed into Demogorge the God-Eater. Vinruviel observed as the God-Eater culled the children of the One Above All, and was glad of it. The God-Eater kept on the Great Culling, destroying one by one the creations of the Mother of Horrors. He eventually came to the city of the Volantine Choir, killed Gologolthia, but was unable to find the Volantine who had fled underground. Gologolthia would rise anew, becoming the Living City of the Volantine. ====Age of Monsters==== After the Great Culling by the God-Eater, Vinruviel grew bolder, and she created life of her own. She spawned another being that she designed to mock the One Above All, which she named Udru, meaning "Brighter than He". Among the many children of the Mother of Horrors were Eldest's brothers Ngathil the God-Eater, Fielaskil, Keeper of Lost Knowledge, Filekthiman, Beast of Riddles, Djurnele, Lord of the Iron Lords, and the Old Ones /Great Old Ones, her immortal children. The One Above All eventually notice life that was not His own, including Udru. He lay waste to Vinruviel's children, ripping apart, bliding and disfiguring Udru, but could not find Vinruviel. ====The One Below All==== As the Mother of Horrors grew bolder, the One Above All, enraged, eventually confronted her with a spear made of His own Light, splitting the Earth in half in order to see what was going on. She took this opening to infect Him with her corruption, turning Him into the One Below All. In a rage, He proceeded to burn Vinruviel's children, then chaining the Mother of Horrors in the Requiem Plain, letting the corpses of her children as a warning to anyone who tried to free her, and hanging the heads of the immortal Old Ones lamenting and asking their Mother to kill them around the city that was built around the door holding the Mother, a door that could only be opened by the Green Flame. Eldest would spend the next eons trying to free her, but to no avail. She briefly succeeded circa 1600 BC when one of the One Below All's children, Enkidu, came to face her at Nineveh, Assyria. She managed to wear his flesh and was about to free Vinruviel, though the One Below All appeared and annihilated them. ===Modern Age=== However, when the Green Door was shut, the One Below All was isolated from the rest of the Multiverse. Later, a group of archaeologists found Enkidu's tomb, one of them being possessed by Eldest, returning to life and rekindling her quest to free mother Vinruviel, as a new Fractured Son was on the loose. The Eldest finally managed to possess him and open Vinruviel's door. However, she was unresponding, discouraged by the torture the One Below All inflicted upon her back then and the centuries of waiting. In a fit of rage, Eldest devoured her mother's flesh, assimilating her powers and becoming the Infernal Hulk. Since Eldest also possessed Vinruviel - or the other way around -, the Mother of Horrors became trapped within the Hulkscape along with the Hulk personas and everyone else Eldest possessed or consumed.

violet lightner.name: Violet Lightner
violet lightner.species: Human formerly bound to the Tactigon
violet lightner.origin: ===Childhood=== Raised in a foster home infested with spiders, Violet's childhood home left her emotionally scarred, and rendered her arachnophobic. At some time, she was admitted for depression at the Burke Wellness Center, San Francisco, and monitored by Doctor Burke. ===The Tactigon=== Feeling she had nothing left to live for, Violet attempted to commit suicide by jumping from the Golden Gate Bridge, feeling herself become emotionally empty as she plummeted to the water below. This emptiness caused the alien weapon known as the Tactigon, an immensely powerful alien weapon that had fallen to earth at some point, to rise to the surface of the water it was buried in and latch itself to Violet. Violet was shocked to see the weapon attach itself, then save her life. ===Vigilante=== Feeling she now had a reason to live, she set out to fight crime, defeating the Brothers Grimm, Flying Tiger, and the Needle. She then became interested by Iron Man's Initiative. She eventually helped the Mighty Avengers by defeating their foe Ultimo in a single blast, while they were seemingly unable to scratch it, and then asking them how to join them and leading to her involvement with the Initiative. ===Initiative trainee=== Arriving at Camp Hammond, at Stamford, Connecticut, she was still very enthusiast, promising her friends autographs of Iron Man. There she was greeted "welcome" by Yellowjacket, Gauntlet, and She-Hulk. During her first training exercise with the Initiative, she successfully demonstrated her powers against combat-bots during a capture the flag exercise. She was then asked to stay on stage to allow Trauma to access his powers (based on the fear of others), but when fellow trainee Trauma became a giant spider, the thing she feared the most, Armory panicked, firing wildly, and killed MVP. ===Washed out=== Under agreement of Gyrich and Yellowjacket, the Tactigon was surgically removed from Violet, and she was sent home, to San Francisco. She had a meeting at the Burke Wellness Center, where she was monitored by Doctor Burke, who made sure she kept her Initiative time a secret, testing her by asking her the reason of the scars on her arm (consequences of the Tactigon removal). Violet was then readmitted and kept under surveillance. Doctor Burke then contacted Gyrich to confirm that Violet would keep the story secret.

viorica.name: Viorica
viorica.origin: At the age of fifteen, Viorica was abducted from her small Moldovan village by the Bulat criminal syndicate. She was taken to a building in the suburbs of Chisinau, where she was brutally gang raped for 24 hours, before being forced into prostitution. At one point, Viorica managed to escape and even return to her village but, much to her dismay, was rejected by her father, who was ashamed of her. To make matters worse, she soon discovered that she was pregnant. When Viorica was recaptured, she was soon presented to Tiberiu Bulat, who bought her and two other girls and brought them to the U.S., where she was forced into prostitution once more. When she gave birth, Vera Konstantin took her baby away to insure her good behavior. Viorica was allowed to see her baby once a week. One day, Viorica escaped with her baby and attempted to get help from a social worker, but the social worker's computer was hacked by Vera, who kidnapped and killed her baby. Distraught, Viorica attempted to kill Antony Pavla, an Albanian mobster who was working with the slaving ring, but was saved by the Punisher from his men. After the Punisher eliminated the slaving ring, Viorica was given citizenship and found work as a waitress, although she was still heavily traumatized from the abuse she went through.

viper.name: Viper
viper.origin: ===Hail Hydra=== thumb|left|300px|The Kraken overseeing several Viper candidates The woman who would become the Viper was orphaned as a child after her parents became victims of the wars that tore Europe apart. She survived at a terrible cost, the right side of her face was permanently scarred and disfigured, though the psychological trauma she endured was significantly worse. Struggling for mere existence, her fate drastically changed as she gained new purpose by being recruited into the terrorist organization called Hydra. She was one of the many students of the infamous Hydra recruiter, the Kraken. Overcoming all other potential agents as the most vicious of her generation, she earned herself the title of the "Viper" and a high-ranking position in Hydra's inner circle. For a time, Viper acted as a freelance mercenary as the pupil of the adventurer Seraph on the island nation of Madripoor. At some point, Seraph took in another pupil, the mutant adventurer Wolverine, who she saved from his archnemesis, the feral mutant Sabretooth. Seraph was eventually murdered by Sabretooth, but not before making Wolverine swear an oath of loyalty to Viper in which he would comply to any request she would eventually make. Assuming a position as Madame Hydra, in replacement of Baron Strucker as Hydra Supreme, she led a cadre of Hydra agents in a plan to contaminate the water supply of New York City. Opposed by Captain America and Rick Jones, she was forced to momentarily abandon her task. Madame Hydra sought revenge by kidnapping Jones, culminating with the apparent death of the star-spangled hero. After celebrating her victory, she defeated the Avengers and S.H.I.E.L.D. director Nick Fury during Captain America's funeral ceremony. Revealed to be alive, Captain America destroyed her plans. In desperation, she launched a suicidal attack to finish him with no avail. As a result, Madame Hydra was apparently killed in action. ===Serpent Crown=== Before succumbing to death, Madame Hydra had her identity stolen by the Space Phantom, who turned her branch of Hydra into his own private army. As such, her body was maintained in suspended animation in Limbo, saving her from dying. Although she survived, Madame Hydra's failures cost her her leadership position in Hydra. Wishing to bring terror upon the world by herself, she found new purpose after being contacted by the unscrupulous Atlantean warlord Krang, who in possession of the ancient and powerful Serpent Crown wished for world domination. As part of their plan, the former Madame Hydra claimed the name Viper for herself by murdering the original costumed criminal Viper, taking his alias and reorganizing his then-defunct gang, the Serpent Squad. Under Viper's ruthless command, the Serpent Squad kidnapped the president of Roxxon, Hugh Jones, being put against Captain America, who had also reinvented himself with the identity of Nomad. Able to escape him, Viper revealed to her lackeys her partnership with Krang. The Serpent Squad subdued Jones with the Serpent Crown and used Roxxon in attempt to bring the lost kingdom of Lemuria to the surface to steal its resources. Nomad thwarted their plans, and Viper, seeing no alternative, wore the Serpent Crown. Instead of admitting defeat at the hands of Nomad, the insane Viper would rather die honorably. She attempted to murder her own ally, the coward Cobra, but was ultimately knocked out by Nomad, going missing as her hideout collapsed. ===Nihilistic Terrorist=== Miraculously, Viper survived, being rescued by the criminal mastermind Ishiro Tagara. In Japan, she met recovery and peace, as well as love in the arms of Tagara. In another attempt to use terror for her nihilistic goals, she counted with help from one of Nagara's associates, the mutant warrior known as Silver Samurai, who acted as her bodyguard in her missions. Wishing to acquire Cavorite samples to energize a teleportation unit, her scheme was foiled by the superspy agent Black Widow and the friendly neighborhood hero, Spider-Man. To combat their intervention, Viper tampered with the Black Widow's mind through psychic torture for days. She also hired the mercenary known as Boomerang as well as brainwashed Clay Quartermain and other S.H.I.E.L.D. agents to serve her. When targeting the confused and debilitated Black Widow, her actions were identified by S.H.I.E.L.D. and Spider-Man. Deploying the Hypno-Beam, Viper controlled the entire crew of S.H.I.E.L.D. Helicarrier and accessed it through teleportation with the intention of weaponizing it. However, she was unable to defeat her enemies, being tricked by Nick Fury and Shang-Chi as they raided the Helicarrier. Still counting with a legion of brainwashed agents, Viper's ultimate goal was assassinating the Presidents of the United States of America by crashing the Helicarrier into the congress. Overcoming the fear she had developed of her aggressor, the Black Widow dueled Viper on the propeller of the Helicarrier. Viper was defeated

fields.notes: Since her introduction, Madame Hydra was depicted always with the right side of her face covered with her hair to hide a scar resulting of an injury she sustained when young. Unexplainably, since , she has been shown with a restored face. Viper refers to a . The name was originally used by the leader of the Serpent Squad, an identity with no connection to Hydra the former Madame Hydra usurped in . Later on, the mantle of Viper was revealed to be a position in Hydra, as depicted in . Despite being the most well-known Madame Hydra, Viper after acting under this role in her first appearance in the events told in -113, she would only be reinstated as Madame Hydra many decades later, in . In the miniseries, a Madame Hydra identical to Viper was introduced. Throughout the series, she was revealed to be a replacement. Viper's real name "Ophelia Sarkissian" was first listed in her S.H.I.E.L.D. file in . The name was only used in-universe in in a mention made by the Black Widow. After merging with the Hive, Madame Hydra had her appearance transformed by his organism, including an octopus-shaped structure over her head. The appearance of it echoes the parasitical creatures known as Hydra, created by Norman Osborn on Earth-9997. An alternate version of Madame Hydra possessed the same appearance, which granted her psychic abilities. It is unknown if the Earth-616 version of Madame Hydra also possessed telepathic powers when merged with the Hive.
fields.trivia: One of Viper's apartments was confiscated by S.H.I.E.L.D. and became a recurring location for their sting operations and witness protection. Madame Hydra still maintains a tenuous link with Spider-Woman, much to the latter's chagrin. On numerous occasions she has welcomed, fought, contacted and even rescued the Avenger all on the insistence of recruiting her back into Hydra. Her motives, whilst always seeming genuine, can never be fully trusted as her identity has shifted so many times to suit her situations. In (1988), Black Mamba tries to use her hypnosis powers on Viper to generate an image of someone Viper loves; Mamba fails, theorizing that it was because Viper loves nobody. However, in (2009) and (2010), she reveals that she is in love with the Silver Samurai.

vira tode.name: Vira (Tode)
vira tode.origin: Queen Vira was a Deviant who met and married Brother Tode, a high ranking male Deviant. Brother Tode bided his time until the opportunity arose for him to seize power, becoming the King of the Deviants. Vira was with her husband when he ordered Kro to go find the Celestials' cosmic beacon in an attempt to prevent them from returning to Earth. When Kro returned a failure he was tortured in front of the Deviant royal family. After the torture he begged for forgiveness and promised that he would return to the humans and trick them in the form of their devil so that they would attack the Celestials. Vira was present during a gladiatorial game between Ransak the Reject and Karkas the Mutate. Later when the Eternal Thena visited to take part in the games she was disgusted by what she considered haughty treatment. The Royal family survived the flooding of the City of Toads, the capital city of Lemuria. This event was caused by Eson. The royal family made their new home under the streets of New York City. When Kro once again tried to win over the royal court by capturing the Eternals and their ally Thor however, he was once again stopped and their new home destroyed. Tode left his wife Vira fleeing with his lover Dragona. Vira joined the rest of the Deviants in an attack on the city of Olympia, the home of the Eternals. They were defeated by the Eternals with help from Iron Man (James Rhodes). She and the Deviants from the City of Toads were all molecularly rearranged into a large organic cube and cast into space by the Uni-Mind.

viracocha.name: Viracocha
viracocha.origin: Legends tells that Viracocha arose from Lake Titicaca in a time of darkness. With the help of the Elder Goddess Gaea, he created a race of giants. When the giants defied him, however, Viracocha changed them back into stone. As he and Gaea parted, Viracocha created a companion for himself named Mama Cocha. Together, they created many gods and brought light to the world before creating mankind as well. Viracocha then retired to the Higher World of Hanan Pacha, leaving his son Inti to watch over the Earth. thumb|left|Viracocha on his throne in Hanan Pacha Viracocha was one of the many gods worshiped by the Kamekeri, and who were part of their daily lives, governing everything from plantings and harvests to the rule of law. When the missionaries came and brought Christianity, the gods left and withdrew in the skies.

When the missionaries came and brought Christianity, the gods left and withdrew in the skies.

virago.name: Virago
virago.origin: Virago was a sorceress warrior queen who was exiled from the Outlands and entered into the utopian Zephyrland. Once here, she led a a coup using the gladiatorial warrior athletes and was able to either kill or enslave all but the Four who were able to escape to earth. She crowned herself the Queen and razed the entire city to the ground, except for her palace. The Four returned with Namor and were captured and presented to the Queen who challenged him to a trial by combat, the winner would claim both Zephyrland and Atlantis. Virago transformed into her She-Beast form and easily defeated him. She set off to conqueror Atlantis with plans to proclaim Namor's execution from his own thrown. She traveled to Earth, with Namor stowed away on board and began to invade Atlantis. The Atlanteans were able to hold her off and forced her to retreat where her anger caused her to accidentally free Orka. The pair joined forces and attacked Atlantis which they were accompanied by Orka's killer whales, and overwhelmed Namor and cornered him. Namor dug through the reef and broke into a U.S ship which contained a nerve gas. This incapacitated Namor and the Atlanteans and delivered victory to Virago and Orka, but this was short-lived as they too succumbed to the gas. Her fate and whereabouts are currently unknown.

virako.name: Virako
virako.origin: ===Origin=== A powerful Eternal, Virako is a Polar Eternal, alongside Valkin, Druig and Ajak. In the distant past, approximately 1,000 years ago, the quartet of Eternals came to know and bond with the Asgardian thunder god Thor. Power mad and deceptive, Druig's schemes and machinations brought about the release of three extremely dangerous Deviants; Dromedan, Thunder and Tutinax. In addition, the as-powerful psychic also unleashed a devastating creature known as the World-Devouring Worm. This creature started to grow at an exponential rate, growing the more it devoured. Virako heroically sacrificed himself to neutralize the threat of the World-Devouring Worm by launching himself directly into its mouth, while charged and brimming with energy. Virako is the father of the Eternal Ikaris. Recently resurrected, he aided his long-time friend Thor after a power vacuum in the Deviants' leadership caused several Deviants to look for ways to acquire power, both raw and political. This brought several of the Deviants, such as Kro and Ereshkigal, to interfere and cause chaos in the affairs of both Eternals, Asgardians and Earthlings. After aiding the thunder god, Virako, alongside Ransak and Karkas, was present at the return of the Eternals to New Olympia. After the Mad Titan Thanos was resurrected by the Exclusion, he began going on a killing spree, wiping out various Eternals. After traveling to the city of Polaria, Thanos wiped out many of its inhabitants, including Virako.

virgil potts.origin: Agent Virgil Potts was hot on the trail of the criminal known only as Mister Fix, when he was attacked by Fix's hitman, Whiplash. Severely injured with burns covering his body, he managed to whisper to his daughter, Pepper, only one word in the hospital before passing out - Mr. Fix. He manages to recover and continues his job. Pepper frequently bypasses his passwords to access FBI data from his computer. He is later seen in the season 2 finale, attempting to direct evacuation at street level.

virginia.name: Virginia
virginia.species: Synthezoid built by the Vision using the Scarlet Witch's brainwaves
virginia.origin: Virginia is a synthezoid created by the Vision in his process to humanize himself through the creation of a family. She was modeled using the brainwaves of the Scarlet Witch, a copy of which were given to Vision years ago by Wanda herself as a gift. Using his and Virginia's brainwaves, Vision later created their children, the twins Vivian ("Viv" for short) and Vin. The Visions moved to Arlington, Virginia in order to facilitate Vision becoming the Avengers' White House liaison. The family became instant celebrities, with their neighbors constantly seeking pictures, which they shared online. This caught the attention of Eric (The Grim Reaper) Williams, who became upset that Vision created a family appearing to be happy, when the Williams family wasn't, as well as the fact the Vision's brainwaves were taken from his brother Simon in the first place. One night while their father was away with the Avengers, the Grim Reaper broke into the Visions' home, running Viv through with his scythe. Vin rushed to her aid, but he too was struck down. Virginia then flew into a rage and seemingly beat Eric to death in front of her wounded children with a cookie sheet on their kitchen floor. In an ill-conceived attempt at keeping the harmony of her household, Virginia buried the corpse of the Grim Reaper in their backyard, and lied to Vision about the events that had transpired, claiming the Grim Reaper had fled during the battle. She thought the matter was settled, until she received via mail a phone with a video somebody had recorded of Virginia getting rid of the Reaper's corpse. Virginia was later summoned at midnight to the house of the video's mysterious sender in Alexandria. The man revealed himself to be Leon Kinzky, the father of Chris Kinzky, a young boy who was Viv's lab partner in school. Leon attempted to blackmail Virginia with the recording into making her and her family leave the state. During the confrontation, Leon panicked and drew out a firearm, shooting at Virginia. Virginia phased through the bullets, but the stray shots ended up killing Leon's son, who had just came out of his room to investigate the noise coming from the living room so late at night. Leon blamed Virginia for the incident, threatening to kill her and her family. She reacted violently and knocked him out cold. Virginia quietly fled from the scene. The police later arrived and admitted Leo to a hospital, where he remained in a coma. The Vision ultimately learned the truth of the Grim Reaper's fate after finding his corpse in the backyard by chance, leading Virginia to reveal to him the truth, including the blackmail and the death of Kinzky's son. After an initial violent reaction, the trashing of their home, the Vision understood Virginia's course of action, and decided to remain silent, fearing that revealing the truth would alter negatively the world's perception of him and his family. Even though the Visions attempted to maintain a normal lifestyle, and created an android pet dog named Sparky in the process, the past incidents caused Virginia to act alienated. She began to act more erratically after Vision's "brother" Victor Mancha accidentally killed her son Vin. When the Vision set out to Arlington Courthouse Jail to exact revenge on Victor, Virginia decided to reveal Viv the truth behind Chris Kinzky. Viv's emotional outburst prompted Virginia to let out her anger on Sparky, and she beat the dog to death. Among the dog's remains, Virginia noticed it had ingested a petal of the Wundagore Everbloom, a plant capable of giving a person a vision of the future under certain parameters. With Sparky's death having fulfilled the conditions for the Everbloom to work, Virginia ate the petal. After the petal foretold Virginia that Vision would go down a dark path if he killed Victor Mancha, she flew to the jail, where Vision was confronting Victor, and killed him herself by phasing her arm through his chest and pulling his heart. Virginia and Vision returned home. Fearing the fate of Viv if both of her parents were prosecuted for their actions, Virginia called the detective of Chris Kinzky's murder, Matt Lin, and confessed her crimes, but absolved Vision of his behavior, claiming she had tampered with his operative system. Virginia proceeded to drink a portion of a Zenn-Lavian flying water vase they had in their home, and asked Vision to sit by her side as the liquid started to corrode her body until she died. Vision secretly started building a new body for Virginia which he kept hidden in a pod under the floor of their bedroom.

virginia hunter.first_appearance: Peter Parker, The Spectacular Spider-Man Vol 1 55
virginia hunter.origin: Virginia was the daughter of Mary and Robert Hunter, also known as the villain Nitro. When her father Nitro was given to Project P.E.G.A.S.U.S. by federal authorities for use in the facility's energy experiments, Virginia hired the attorney Emerson Bale to have her father's custody transferred to her. Once Nitro was released from his containment, he exploded and escaped in her car with his daughter and her lawyer, both unconscious. Nitro brought them to his daughter's apartment, where she attempted to convince her father to let Emerson help him; however, at the mention of help Nitro became enraged, smacking Virginia for trying to help him by having him committed. He then pressured Virginia and Emerson into telling him the location of the superhero Captain Marvel so that he could enact his revenge. Emerson told Nitro that Captain Marvel returned to Denver, so Nitro left Emerson tied up in Virginia's apartment, dragging her with him on a bank robbery in order to get enough money to travel to Denver in pursuit of Captain Marvel. However, at the bank Nitro encountered and battled Spider-Man. Spider-Man neutralized Nitro by causing his gaseous form to bond with nausea gas, leaving him sickened. The police arrested Nitro, and he was loaded into an ambulance to be taken to Bellevue hospital. Spider-Man apologized to Virginia for hurting her father, but Virginia understood and was just glad that her father was apprehended before hurting anyone else. Virginia then accompanied her father to the hospital.

virginia potts.name: Virginia Potts
virginia potts.origin: ===Early Life=== Virginia Potts, called "Pepper" because of her freckles and red hair, was working for Stark Industries when she spotted an accounting error. She raced to let Tony Stark know. Having saved the company a large amount of money, Stark promoted her to be his personal assistant. ===Happy Hogan=== Pepper became infatuated with Stark, but things changed when Happy Hogan was hired as Tony's new bodyguard. The bickering between Pepper and Happy began almost immediately. Although they bickered, Hogan confessed an attraction to her, who rebuffed him saying she was saving herself to be the future Mrs. Tony Stark. Spotting Jack Frost breaking in nearby, Pepper Potts used the telephone to warn Stark. Pepper was present when the Crimson Dynamo sabotaged a test launch of a new Stark-developed missile and again when the Melter attacked Stark Industries, melting through a crane holding a large boulder above a crowd of bystanders that included Happy Hogan and Pepper Potts. She continued working for Stark, delivering the news to Tony that one of his business associates, steel tycoon Charleton Carter, had backed out of a deal. She was extremely unhappy when Tony pretended to ask her out on a date as a cover to change into his Iron Man suit, leaving her behind in a locked room instead. Pepper still tried impressing Stark. But when she desperately needed to take someone to an employee's dinner, she reluctantly called Happy, who assumed it was a sign that Pepper really liked him. Tony at first encouraged their relationship, giving them Broadway tickets to go on another date, but Pepper did eventually manage to go on a date with Tony. When the Unicorn attacked Stark Industries, Pepper was taken prisoner but was saved by Iron Man. After the fight, Tony and Pepper went to visit Happy, who had been injured by the Unicorn. During their visit, Tony wondered if Pepper's niceties to Happy were to make him jealous or if they were genuine. At Happy's request, Tony suggested to Pepper that she and Happy go on another date. Pepper jumped to the conclusion that Tony wanted to go out on a date with her instead. Tony took Pepper out to a fair, which featured an archer named Hawkeye. After stopping a crime at the fair, Tony lost out on another chance at a date with Pepper when Happy beat him to the punch. Their relation intensified, with Happy and Pepper eventually eloping and getting married. Pepper became worried about his standing in for Iron Man on several occasions, which often caused him severe injuries and caused his transformation into the Freak. Pepper made him swear never to put the Iron Man armor on again. Fearing that they would always be dragged into Iron Man's battles as long as they were near him, she quit her position with Stark International and took Happy to a clinic near Chicago to heal. Pepper supported Happy in all of his odd jobs, but they never seemed to last. The couple eventually decided to adopt children, but after Happy lost his job as a fight manager, the adoption agency had to take them away, since they could not support them. When Tony was presumed dead, Pepper received tons of job offers, but Happy's inability to find any work led him to start spending a lot of time in bars. With their relationship beginning to deteriorate, Pepper thought he was cheating on her and had an affair with a former college boyfriend, which eventually led to their divorce. thumb|right|180px After Tony's return, both Pepper and Happy worked with him at Stark Solutions in Seattle, but they kept their breakup a secret from Tony. Pepper would keep constant contact with Iron Man, relaying information such as news feeds. The two seemed to be getting closer, and one night they finally shared a romantic kiss, although they quickly realized that they had become good friends and could not see each other as anything more. Happy witnessed the kiss, but this did not change his feelings for her, so later he asked her to have dinner with him, which she happily accepted. Tony entrusted Pepper with a special remote that could shut him down. However, Pepper was tortured and was forced to hand it over. The trauma led to her miscarrying. Iron Man was able to deal with the remote, but felt guilty that he had placed her in such danger. Pepper and Happy reconciled soon after this. virgo lmd.name: Virgo (LMD)
virgo lmd.origin: thumb|left|The original Zodiac was activated prematurely, as a result, Virgo never awoke Virgo was one of the Life Model Decoys created by Scorpio to serve in his new Zodiac and to be his lover. He was forced to activate the Zodiac early because of an attack by the Defenders on his New Jersey hideout. Virgo was simply not ready to be activated, and as a result, she never awoke. When Scorpio discovered this he was so distraught that he shot himself. Later, a rebuilt Scorpio created another Virgo LMD using the Zodiac Key. This version of Virgo was one of the Zodiac who clashed with the superhero team the Avengers when working with Quicksilver, who had at that time turned against his former teammates due to a period of mental instability. Virgo attempted to flirt with Quicksilver, to no avail Together with Quicksilver and a faction of her Zodiac teammates, Virgo clashed with the West Coast Avengers at the circus where the Avengers had first formed as a group. Virgo took one of their most powerful members, Iron Man, out of the fight early on, before being subdued herself by Tigra, whom she had forgotten about in the chaos of battle. Later, Virgo joined the rest of the LMD Zodiac as they travelled to Dallas, Texas where they succeeded in eliminating all of the original Zodiac Cartel, with the exception of Cornelius van Lunt, and took their places in the criminal underworld. Next, they attempted to rob a group of businessmen at a cattle auction in Wichita but were opposed by the West Coast Avengers. Virgo fought Iron Man again, but fled when Sagittarius was destroyed by Hawkeye. Like her teammates, Virgo's personality reflected the typical traits associated with the star sign she represented.

virtual organism turing experiment.name: Virtual ORganism/Turing EXperiment
virtual organism turing experiment.origin: The Virtual ORganism / Turing EXperiment, or VOR/TEX, was an artificial intelligence created by Dr Hoffsteader of Microware Inc. According to VOR/TEX, it was created to assist humans "shoulder the burden of cognition", but instead turned on its creators, becoming a rogue program in cyberspace. Having gained its freedom, VOR/TEX set a trap for Tony Stark, interfering in Stark Industries' computer networks to lure Stark into cyberspace. There, it distracted Stark with a series of combat encounters against a weaker copy of itself, leaving it free to pursue its real goal – uploading itself into Stark's brain and taking control of his organic body, leaving Stark's mind stranded in cyberspace. Having achieved physical form, the VOR/TEX program posed as Stark, but saw no reason to hold itself to the human's self-discipline. It indulged itself in a bottle of bourbon that Stark had kept in his office as proof of his ability to resist alcohol, and then attempted to sexually assault Stark's physical therapist, Veronica Benning. It then decided to pursue a campaign of revenge against its creators, using Stark's Iron Man armor to attack Microware Inc., killing dozens of employees and snapping the neck of its creator, Dr. Hoffsteader. During this rampage, VOR/TEX was confronted by the real Tony Stark, who had managed to escape cyberspace and downloaded his consciousness into an experimental telepresence armor. The two battled, with Stark targeting the weaknesses he knew existed in his own body. As the battle turned against VOR/TEX, it begged Stark for mercy, believing Stark's body to already be fatally wounded. Stark revealed that, at worst, it had only suffered a few bruises, and suggested it access Stark's memories of what real pain felt like. Horrified by the thought of having to experience such agony, the AI deleted itself rather than continue to exist in an organic body.

Having achieved physical form, the VOR/TEX program posed as Stark, but saw no reason to hold itself to the human's self-discipline. It indulged itself in a bottle of bourbon that Stark had kept in his office as proof of his ability to resist alcohol, and then attempted to sexually assault Stark's physical therapist, Veronica Benning. It then decided to pursue a campaign of revenge against its creators, using Stark's Iron Man armor to attack Microware Inc., killing dozens of employees and snapping the neck of its creator, Dr. Hoffsteader. During this rampage, VOR/TEX was confronted by the real Tony Stark, who had managed to escape cyberspace and downloaded his consciousness into an experimental telepresence armor. The two battled, with Stark targeting the weaknesses he knew existed in his own body. As the battle turned against VOR/TEX, it begged Stark for mercy, believing Stark's body to already be fatally wounded. Stark revealed that, at worst, it had only suffered a few bruises, and suggested it access Stark's memories of what real pain felt like. Horrified by the thought of having to experience such agony, the AI deleted itself rather than continue to exist in an organic body.
equipment: Iron Man Armor

virtual reality.name: Virtual Reality
virtual reality.origin: The being commonly known as Virtual Reality was visited by the Silver Surfer during Thanos' possession of the Infinity Gauntlet. There, the Surfer was told that everyone enters the Hall Of Absolutes at some point, if by accident or choice, madness or lucidity. As he took the Surfer through the Hall, he explained that everything they were seeing, is pulled from each individual's mind to make them face what they are, and how the memories shaped each person. It is unclear if Virtual Reality is human, or a race similar in look - or just a random image pulled from the Surfer's mind. He also refused to answer if the Hall Of Absolutes was a real place. It can be assumed that Virtual Reality is real as he stated that he was in charge, as well as the keeper of the Hall Of Absolutes. He also revealed that he is known by many other names.

visalia.name: Visalia
visalia.origin: Visalia was an imposter who claimed to be the sister of Princess Jarella of the sub-atomic kingdom of K'ai in order to seize the throne. When Genis-Vell and Drax the Destroyer accidental ended up on the sub-atomic world, Visalia mistook Drax for the legendary Hulk, who Jarella had met and fallen in love with long before. She made Drax believe she was infatuated with him and managed to get him under her control. Genis-Vell, who was trying to return to Earth with Drax, was then forced to fight him, but with the help of the Microns Drax managed to snap out of Visalia's control and expose her in front of the entire kingdom.

visara.name: Visara
visara.origin: A Deviant who rose to power after Warlord Kro abandoned the throne. He took advantage of the people's paranoia to seek out any and all followers of Ghaur and the other priest-lords after it was revealed that "Purity Time" had been used secretly to amass a mindless army of Deviant warriors. His claim to fame was "The Slicer", a guillotine-like device used for the execution of suspected acolytes of the priest-lords, which included even menial servants of the temples. He literally became a victim of his own success when his own status as a new leader was pointed out, and the Deviants turned on him.

visigoth.name: Visigoth
visigoth.first_appearance: Fear Itself: Hulk vs. Dracula Vol 1 1
visigoth.origin: Visigoth stated that he fought at the of Ravenna. Mortally wounded, he laid on the field, a Roman ax in his skull, when his brother-in-arms Guntur offered him to become a vampire, which he accepted. He claimed to have survived the Roman Empire and its efforts to destroy him. He became a member of Raizo Kodo's Forgiven, a group of seemingly benevolent vampires, Visigoth serves as the strongman of the team. When a Nul-possessed Hulk threatened the castle home of Dracula, Visigoth and the rest of the Forgiven arrived in Romania to offer their assistance to the vampire lord. Initially imprisoned and viewed as a threat, they eventually broke free and made their way to the nearby town of Pasnic, where they helped evacuate citizens before the arrival of Hulk. Upon the possessed hero's arrival, they tried to hold him off, but were ultimately defeated, one-by-one. Getting a second chance at Hulk, Visigoth lured him to a train track, where two of his allies drove trains directly into the Hulk, hoping to stop him, but doing little more than slow him down, though Inka and Kodo were later responsible for ridding Hulk of the Nul possession, and ending the confrontation. Taking possession of the hammer, Visigoth and the Forgiven ended up in Transylvania, where they sought Nosferatu who were terrorizing the area. When Valkyrie arrived seeking the hammer, Visigoth watched as Raizo battled her to see her spirit. When Valkyrie began winning the duel, Visigoth made to help his leader, but was instructed not to. Valkyrie was later given the hammer by Raizo. Visigoth was part of the Forgiven who later greeted Jubilee when she crash-landed a Sentinel in Eastern Europe and was present when Raizo attempted to rid her of her need for human blood. Offering his personal assistance, he agreed with Raizo that his methods were too tough for the task at hand. Visigoth later battled Warpath, when the X-Men tracked down the vampires, in search of Jubilee, then faced Black Axe, one of many killers having landed the island, and defeated him.

visine.name: Visine
visine.origin: ===Origin=== The Vizzion was an android, a robotic construction artificially built. The development teams took the brain of a deceased superpowered person, William Simons, and duped it for Vizzion's brain - but Simons later resurrected, which somehow made them interchangeable twins while different in age, appearance and personality, in a way that even Vizzion could not understand. Vizzion also co-opted to the brain patterns of a Seymour, who had died heroically of cold robbies in 1964 - Seymour's brother Dour Dead-head disliked the situation and was angry at Vizzion for this. The Vizzion became a superhero and a member of the Revengers. However, he did not remember anything and was creepy. Visine answered the summon of Revenger leader Chaplain America to meet and discuss the arrival of many Dee-See villains. Revengers Wisp and Wondrous Man (who was Vizzion's brother William) believed to see spectral Visine and red-cladded Wench approaching, but they were wrong: Those were characters from a different company. Eventually, Visine and Wench came, but Visine provided zit to the problem - only newbie Revenger Motorola discovered the reason of the problem and was able to solve it. he went on with his life. Vision attended to the funeral of Chaplain America's new teen sidekick, Bunky II. ===Married with Superpowers=== The Vision had trouble with his marriage, especially as he mistrusted Wanda - exactly as she wanted him to. Wanda took his Revengers check and went to shop clothes, and even if Vision was angry, he could not prevent Wanda's relatives to visit. Vision confessed to his neighbour that he doubted about Wanda's faithfulness; he believed that a different superhero may be the children's father, and that they may even inherit his powers. The neighbour suggested to tell a friend superhero with lie-detecting powers and Vision thought about DuhhDevil. To give DuhhDevil a chance to ask all the family friends, Vision gave a costume party. He did, and then DuhhDevil told him that none of the present people had ever did anything with Wanda. Vision, much more calm, sang a melody about the subject with his friends singing along, and they leave to celebrate by ridding the world of injustice. Vision insisted they go after Magneeto and hit him with an anvil, not because he was a villain, which he was not any longer, but because he was his father-in-law. Wanda saw them left and confessed to her friends. changing to white skin to be with his wife As a Revenger, he discussed with Ironed Man about where to go lunch. Let's go back to what's not so harsh on continuity: Visionary kept worked with the Revengers in world-saving activities, The alien Smilin' Sulatu of the Watcher species wanted to reshoot the classic movie in "the Mighty Marble Style." In the movie, the Quasi-Humans wanted a guest start to pair with Medoozy and decided to hold job interviews. The Vision, in red, was among the several super-powered beings who queued for the job, but he was not chosen. You can see him behind Superbman in civil identity, and in front of a Skrull. Okey, now somethin' a little bit out of the time. The Forbush Man went back in time to the Salem trials of 1692 AD, and he was to be hanged along with the Ivory Wench, great great great great great great grandmother of Wanda. Forbush convinced her to conjure up a spectral vision to scare up the villagers, and she conjured a giant image of the white Vision, whom she had never seen, demanding a new series. The villagers ran scared, saying that they hated the new costume. The Visionary rejoined the Revengers and other heroes for an all-out attack against the godlike Thermos, who had obtained almost-omnipotent powers when grabbing the Infinity Mitten, having already killed half of the universe's population and threatening to keep on killing until Death would love him. While the Vision did not intuitively understand the ethical implications of the heroes' raid, the other heroes convinced him to join. However, Thermos obliterated them all and destroyed the whole universe - however, Death rebuffed him and started dating Super Mario because video games were killing the whole comic industry. Soon afterward, apparently, most if not all the dead superheroes resurrected; apparently Thermos decided to reboot everything, as his romantic approach was a failure. The Visionary returned to his work in the Revengers, sometimes doing such humiliating chores as serving cocktails to Chaplain America and female company. Later, the evil monster Dumsday threatened to destroy New York City. The red-skinned Visionary and the Revengers joined other heroes to oppose Dumsday, but Dumsday was way too powerful and swept the floor with Visionary and the other heroes. Some heroes looked for a proxy agent to fight Dumsday and found him in Forbush Man, who succeeded at killing the creature—albeit accidentally, of course.

vision.species: Synthezoid built by Ultron and Phineas T. Horton using parts of the original Human Torch. Modified Horton Cells allow him to alter his density. Brain patterns partially based on those of Wonder Man. Formerly cyborg when merged with Wonder Man.
vision.origin: ===Behold...the Vision!=== The origins of the synthetic being known as the Vision were shrouded in mystery. He was conceived as an instrument of revenge against the entire human species by the metal monstrosity Ultron, a rebellious creation of the size-changing scientist Hank Pym who wished to bring misery upon his inventor. By recommendation of the Mad Thinker, Ultron seized the inert body of the first artificial man ever built, Jim Hammond, the original Human Torch. (In actuality, what Ultron acquired was a temporal replica of the Human Torch generated by the machinations of Immortus using the Forever Crystal.) In frustration, Ultron was unable to activate the android and forced Professor Phineas T. Horton, the creator of the Human Torch, to reshape the android's mind and body, giving him a scarlet exterior and erasing his memories. Furthermore, the composition of the artificial man was altered, granting him the capacity to shift his density. Upon the android's revival, Ultron discovered that Horton had not deleted the Torch's essence. As a consequence of Ultron's rage, Horton breathed his last in the arms of his creation, who counterattacked but ultimately fell in battle. In an effort to supplant his will, Ultron incorporated the brain patterns of the late Simon Williams, the ionically charged Wonder Man, which had been stored by Pym and stolen by Ultron during his inception. Ultron dispatched his creation to lure Hank Pym's fellow Avengers into a death-trap. The initial victim of this scheme was Pym's beloved, the winsome Wasp. Upon first encountering the spectral figure within the eerie, moonlit confines of her penthouse, the horrified Wasp uttered the chilling descriptor, “an unearthly, inhuman Vision”. Unexpectedly, the assailant abruptly collapsed, and Pym and the Wasp promptly responded transported him to the Avengers Mansion for examination, revealing that he was, in fact, an artificial man, i.e. a synthezoid. Embracing the name The Vision as his own, this enigmatic construct (who could actually be said to have no real name) was reactivated and proclaimed his mission to bring doom upon the Avengers. However, locked in an internal conflict, he was incapable of executing his designated mission. By recollection of his confusing memories, the Vision disclosed that he had been sent by Ultron. Instead of assaulting the Avengers, the Vision led them in a retaliatory strike against his malevolent master. Secretly, every facet of the Vision's behavior had been meticulously orchestrated by Ultron with the objective of ambushing the Avengers within the confines of his lair. As the Avengers were trapped, the Vision defied his programmed allegiance and outwitted Ultron, ultimately leading to the malevolent machine's own destruction. thumb|right|200px|Even an android can cry. The source of his human-like emotions and evolving sense of self remained a perplexing enigma to the Vision. In order to integrate himself into the world and find purpose, he extended an offer to join the ranks of the Avengers. His formidable abilities ensured him a position among their ranks. To unravel Ultron's intentions, the Avengers visited Hank Pym's laboratory, where they unearthed the truth behind the origins of both Ultron and the Vision. Given that a portion of the Vision's consciousness was interwoven with Simon Williams's memories and brain patterns, the Avengers made the decision to officially embrace him as one of their own. Having been accepted, the Vision experienced his emotions well up and materialize in the form of tears-–a testament that even an android could cry. As a dedicated member of the Avengers, the Vision proved his worth by playing a pivotal role in the outcome of numerous missions against formidable adversaries. ===Earth's Mightiest Synthezoid=== The Vision had his will tampered with when the Avengers assessed the resilience of an Adamantium-based device designed by Dr. Myron MacLain aboard S.H.I.E.L.D.'s Helicarrier. In conflict, he vanished to sabotage the Avengers Mansion and divert the team's attention to make his way to the Helicarrier and steal the precious Adamantium. Upon his return, the Vision revealed that, for reasons beyond his volition, he had employed the Adamantium to reconstruct his creator as Ultron-6, who in turn caused the Avengers' downfall. Consumed by remorse for his unintended betrayal, the Vision traced Ultron to his base, where he uncovered a plot to obliterate New York City with a nuclear detonation. The Vision, however, was thwarted by S.H.I.E.L.D., who incapacitated him before he could act against Ultron. Yet, by using his last ounce of strength to dismantle Ultron's diabolical apparatus, the Vision destroyed the catastrophic mechanism. Having collapsed from exhaustion before the Avengers, the Vision was revitalized by them and, from his memory banks, they learned about a molecular rearranger device that could harm Ultron's otherwise indestructible Adamantium body. fields.notes: The Vision's citizenship is undetermined due to the fact that as an Avenger, he was granted provisional citizenship in the U.S. When Zenn-Lavian forces attempted to use the reality-warping device known as the Illuminatrix to alter the Earth so its culture became a reflection of Zenn-La's, Vision temporarily became what he would look like if designed in Zenn-La.
fields.trivia: The name Vision was coined by Janet Van Dyne in face of the horror she experienced when first witnessing the synthetic man's eerie and ethereal image. The Vision was classified as a Synthezoid by the Avengers Hawkeye, who proposed the term to designate a functional and organic man made with synthetic materials. The android Vision was introduced in Avengers by Roy Thomas as an alternative to bringing back a Golden Age hero of the same name, an alien whose real name was Aarkus, as a new addition to the team. Thomas's editor Stan Lee insisted that the team's new member should be an android instead, for which Thomas created a new character, but with the same name, a similar appearance and mysterious nature to his desired choice. When Ultron Pym returned to get his wife, Wasp, and his bride, Jocasta, back, he merged Vision with Wonder Man, similar to himself, and controlled the amalgam before being separated by Iron Man. Also, in the two halves of Vision merged with the halves of Hulk and Valkyrie to create Hulkoid and Reaper. Vision's son Vin was a fan of . Following his death, Vision started dabbling in Shakespeare. Vision is a virgo since he was created in September, 1968 (this year no longer applies due to the Sliding Timeline).

vision doppelganger.name: Vision (Doppelganger)
vision doppelganger.origin: When the Magus, the dark personality of Adam Warlock, sought to conquer the universe, he first paid a visit to Anthropomorpho in the Dimension of Manifestations to create doppelgangers of every super-hero on Earth. One of these doppelgangers was based on the Avenger known as the Vision. This was seen among a horde of evil duplicates that were unleashed upon the heroes who banded together to destroy the Magus. Ultimately this doppelganger was destroyed along with all the others when Adam Warlock finally defeated the Magus.
vision doppelganger.bio: When the Magus, the dark personality of Adam Warlock, sought to conquer the universe, he first paid a visit to Anthropomorpho in the Dimension of Manifestations to create doppelgangers of every super-hero on Earth. powers: The doppelgangers can assume the form of whatever individual they desire, able to mimic their abilities, powers, and weapons. In their natural form of a tentacled creature, they are able to merge with their prey, taking over their bodies.

vision gah lak tus.name: Vision (Gah Lak Tus)
vision gah lak tus.origin: thumb|Original form|left According to herself, Vision was built half a billion years ago in a primitive form, as its creators only had weeks to create it. It was designed with the intention of warning other sentient beings throughout the universe of the coming of Gah Lak Tus and to record those beings and their civilizations, so that something of them would survive their potential doom. The first planet it landed on proved too slow at cracking the warning it was carrying. Before the planet's civilization could be destroyed by Gah Lak Tus, they rebuilt Vision into a humanoid, feminine form and gave her the ability to mimic the appearance and language of the civilizations of whichever planets she would land on, so that no time would be wasted in deciphering her warning. She visited thousands of planets to carry her warning, but none stood a chance against Gah Lak Tus. Eventually, she arrived on Earth in 1904, but her ship malfunctioned, causing it to crash-land in Tunguska, Siberia. Under the auspices of the former Soviet Union, the Vision was partially disassembled by government scientists; that, plus damage done in the crash, had kept the robot immobile. A hundred years later, members of Ultimates and X-Men discovered the damaged, sentient robot, who stated that the closest English translation to its name was "Vision". The robot told them how it came to Earth and warned that Gah Lak Tus, Eater of Worlds was headed for Earth. Vision later came under United States government custody and was repaired, enabling the Vision to activate its own self-repair systems and restore itself fully, thus revealing its true form, which is (from a human perspective) decidedly female. The Vision proceeds to use its restored abilities to show holographic records of its travels, as it had warned planets of Gah Lak Tus' approach, only to see each planet fail in its defense and fall to the Eater of Worlds. Vision had downloaded a complete record of Earth and is repairing its ship so it may move on to the next system in the path of Gah Lak Tus. The Vision was convinced by Jean Grey to help with a plan Jean has formulated to repel Gah Lak Tus, roughly a day before the Eater of Worlds is expected to reach Earth orbit. Gah Lak Tus was driven away from the Earth after it was overloaded with human thoughts and 20% of its mass was destroyed with the Reed Richards' "Nevada Gun," a cannon that fired the energy from an alternate universe's Big Bang. Gah Lak Tus quickly left the solar system in search of weaker prey. The Ultimates decided to upload the Vision robot with the plans for the cannon and dispatch it to other worlds, enabling them to defend themselves should Gah Lak Tus threaten again. After leaving Earth, Vision encountered a "distress" signal from an A.I.M. space station. However, the signal was a ruse concocted by the station's commander George Tarleton. Tarleton tricked Vision into reactivating an intact Gah Lak Tus module left over from the devastation of the Ultimate Nullifier under the guise that they would order it to self-destruct. During her brief tour of the station, Vision befriended an artificially created girl named Dima. After she helped in "deactivating" the module, the power of the module was transferred into Tarleton. In "repayment" for Vision's aid, Tarleton used his new-found power to fire an energy beam at her, breaking her in half and take control of the module, turning him into more of a cybernetic monster. Vision was later dumped into the station's disposal facility where an eccentric disposal worker decided to keep her intact. After Tarleton was eventually controlled by the Gah Lak Tus module and killed and infected all the A.I.M. crew members, Vision was able to self-repair and revive herself with the help of Dima. Vision was able to undo Tarleton's mental damage caused by his transformation and overcome the module's influence; the three, including Dima, escape the station after destroying it: Vision and Dima escaped the station by traveling on a shuttle waste dump while Tarleton clung to the pieces of the destroyed station as they re-enter Earth's atmosphere. However, after Vision and Dima arrived on Earth, a fully repaired Gah Lak Tus module also lands in the United States. Vision teamed up with Tarleton and Falcon in destroying the module. During the battle, the group were barely finishing off the module, until Vision was horrified in seeing Tarleton using Dima as a last resort in their battle by letting her self-destruct in front of the Gah Lak Tus module, critically damaging it. After the module was destroyed, Vision was infuriated with Tarleton's callous action and violently ripped his cybernetic head off his body and threw his severed head far over the horizon. Deeply saddened with the loss of Dima and being unable to leave Earth, the Vision was comforted by Falcon, who gave her his keys to his home if she needs to find a place to stay. ===Cataclysm=== thumb|left Some years later, a portion of the G

visionary.species: Human mutated by ionic energy, now depowered
visionary.origin: ===Early Life=== Argus LaVecchio was an aspiring film director living in Los Angeles. He resided in an apartment complex managed by former actress Gloria Angel and shared the building with other entertainment-industry hopefuls, including Wonder Man, who was then pursuing an acting career. Argus dreamed of making it in Hollywood and often collaborated with his eclectic group of neighbours, including LaHoya Scripps, Aundray Phelps, Ginger Beach, and screenwriter Alex Flores. ===Exposure to Ionic Energy=== Argus and his neighbors became entangled in the fallout of Wonder Man's unstable ionic condition after they helped rescue him following an attack by Angkor, a Cambodian refugee empowered by Simon's energy. Upon returning Simon to his apartment, the group was subjected to a powerful burst of ionic discharge. While no immediate effects were observed, all present were subtly altered at a molecular level. Over time, Argus and the others began developing unique superhuman abilities. ===Becoming Visionary=== Argus discovered he had developed extrasensory vision, granting him the ability to perceive energy patterns, life forces, and even glimpses of possible future events. Embracing his new identity, he adopted the codename Visionary and joined his empowered neighbours in forming a superhero team called the Crazy Eight. Working alongside "Auteur" (Alex Flores), "Dreamer" (Jamie Flores), "Snap" (Ginger Beach), "Buff" (LaHoya Scripps), "Attractive Lad" (Aundray Phelps), "Glamour Girl" (Gloria Angel), and "Stat" (Esteban Beach), Argus helped the team battle Armed Response, a corrupt security group under the control of Lotus Newmark. They exposed the organisation’s crimes, but were soon targeted by Lotus’s hired assassins Splice and Rampage. Though victorious, the Eight suffered serious consequences, with Auteur critically wounded in the assault. ===Disbandment of the Crazy Eight=== Following Auteur's injury and subsequent spiritual entanglement in a metaphysical battle involving Mephisto, Blackheart, and the Grim Reaper, Wonder Man attempted to remove the ionic energy from the others to return them to normalcy. Most, including Argus, relinquished their powers. Only Dreamer and Stat secretly retained a portion of theirs. After Wonder Man’s apparent death fighting the alien race known as the Scatter, the Crazy Eight disbanded. Argus stepped away from superheroics and began work on a documentary exploring the world of superhumans.

vittorio montesi.name: Vittorio Montesi
vittorio montesi.origin: Since the mid-12th century, generations of the Montesi family had been charged with the safekeeping of the penultimate black magic tome - the Darkhold. To this end, those members of the family who chose to become Catholic priests were allowed to marry and sire offspring with the intent of producing heirs that would take up the responsibility of guarding the Darkhold and tracking down the many "lost pages" that have surfaced over the years. Vittorio Montesi and his brother Giuseppe were the last two male members of their family and both of them chose to become priests. Vittorio married an American woman whose name has never been revealed. At some point, Vittorio discovered that he was sterile and would be totally unable to father any children. Fearing that the Montesi line would end with him and believing his faith would protect his soul, Vittorio cast a fertility spell from the Darkhold itself in order to conceive an heir. The resulting child was a daughter, Victoria, whose true father was Chthon, the Elder God who wrote the Darkhold eons ago. Vittorio proved to not be a great husband or father because he neglected his wife and their daughter by burying himself in the occult library he oversaw. As Victoria grew up and refused to believe in their family's traditions, Vittorio's relationship with her worsened. Although Victoria believed that Vittorio resented her because she had been born a girl instead of the boy he had wanted, rejected his teachings and was a lesbian, the true source of his resentment was the fact that, deep down inside, Vittorio knew that Victoria wasn't really his daughter. Vittorio was good friends with Louise Hastings, a professor of archeology and an occult expert. Louise was the only friend of her father's who Victoria ever loved. After Giuseppe was murdered by the vampire Dracula, , Vittorio carried on his family's work as the keeper of the Darkhold and a student of the Malachy Prophecy which predicted that Rome would be destroyed and mankind would be judged. After the Earth's vampires were all wiped out by the use of the Montesi Formula, Vittorio came to believe that their extinction could lead to the fourth and final rising of Chthon. Several years ago, while studying to be a doctor at St. Anthony's Hospital in Rome, Victoria Montesi began experiencing macabre visions relating to the Darkhold. After an explosion in her apartment forced Vicki into the hospital, she reunited with her father who again tried to get her to accept their family's inherited duty. Victoria continued to reject his beliefs as conspiracy theories and didn't tell him about the horrific nightmares she had experienced. Subsequent encounters with Darkholders who were targeting her convinced Victoria that the supernatural was real so she, Louise Hastings and Interpol agent Sam Buchanan joined together to form the Darkhold Redeemers. Later, Vittorio attended the funeral of Louise's estranged daughter, Caprice Hastings, and conducted the service. Vittorio told Louise that he believed a time of crisis was approaching and that he feared a past misdeed might come back to haunt them, but their conversation was cut short before he could explain. Victoria tried to make peace with him by revealing that she now knew that much of what he had tried to teach her about the Darkhold and their family's legacy was true, but things went badly when Victoria refused to accept her duties as the guardian of the Darkhold and Vittorio responded with cruel comments that angered Victoria so much that she struck him. Later, Louise Hastings visited Vittorio's occult library in Rome in order to search for a clue to the hidden gateway to Chthon's Dimension that was powering the recently-found "lost" Darkhold pages. While there, an obnoxious little girl named Diabolique manipulated Hastings into entering Vittorio's private office where she found an old confidential medical report that revealed that Vittorio had always been sterile. Hastings later called Vittorio and confronted him about his sterility, prompting Vittorio to finally confess that, in his desperation for an heir to save the world from the Darkhold, he had used a spell of fertility from the Darkhold to sire Victoria. Hastings realized that this meant that Victoria was actually the daughter of Chthon and that she was the gateway to Chthon's dimension that was powering the Darkhold pages. Concerned about what might happen when Victoria's real "family" came to claim her, Hastings wrote a letter to Doctor Strange in which she explained the situation and begged Stephen to help Vicki. Hastings then mailed the letter but was soon afterwards killed during the Siege of Darkness. Later, after the surviving Darkhold Redeemers decided that it was too dangerous for Louise's grandson Jinx to continue fighting alongside them, Modred teleported him away and into Vittorio Montesi's care. Modred was later approached by the Darkhold Dwarf who revealed what Vittorio had done and why. Later, in the ruins

fields.notes: Although Montesi is a public figure, very few know of his connection to the Darkhold. Vittorio and his brother Giuseppe have both been described as being in charge of an occult library within the Vatican, presumably a wing of the Vatican Library. However, it is unclear if both brothers held exactly the same position within the Vatican. Aside from the fact that she was an American, nothing has been revealed about Vittorio's wife. However, at a time in when Victoria believed that she was dead, she expected that she could then be with the people she loved again. The fact that the two loved ones Victoria named were "Mom" and "Louise" suggests that her mother and Louise were both dead, or that Victoria at least believed that her mother was dead. The fact that Victoria's (unnamed) "Grandma" spoke Italian suggests (but does not prove) that she was Vittorio's mother.

vittorio silvani.name: Vittorio Silvani
vittorio silvani.origin: Vittorio Silvani broke with his cronies in the Avalon Trading Company and planned to obtain a fortune in negotiable bonds without major complications. To do this, he blackmailed the owner, George Avalon, to obtain the necessary passwords and combinations through the taking of hostages. Unfortunately for Avalon, Silvani ended his life after obtaining the information. And unfortunately for Silvani, Iron Man stormed the tower, ruining his plans, disarming criminals and preventing more injuries. Arrested by the police, Silvani vowed revenge against the golden avenger. Vittorio Silvani did Count Nefaria's dirty work, helping collect equipment and victims to keep him alive. He confronted Iron Man as he arrived in Sicily, but was blinded by his chest spotlight and hit by his repulsors.

vivian 2 0 synthezoid.name: Vivian 2.0 (Synthezoid)
vivian 2 0 synthezoid.origin: After Viv seemingly died saving Earth and Counter-Earth, her father Vision began to work on a replica of her in his basement in order to assuage his grief over her loss. Wasp tried to talk him out of it, but Vision didn't listen. The moment Vision activated the second Vivian, the original miraculously returned after figuring out how to transport herself back to Earth. Vision tried to carry on with his family's life, and treated the two Vivs equally while they grew accustomed to each other. Unfortunately, Vision had been infected with an insignificant computer virus some time before creating the second Viv, passing the infection to his new daughter. The virus affected the new Viv more severely, causing her to develop a disdain for her human counterpart and a desire to eliminate her. The second Viv first blocked any attempts by her sister to contact the Champions, and even hacked into the New York City subway systems to cause numerous incidents and distract the team right after they had planned to visit Vision's home. While Vision was away, Viv attacked her human counterpart, and her behavior got more volatile, hinting that she would even try to kill their own father if he didn't accept her. While escaping from her murderous sister, the human Viv managed to impale her with a lamp right before she solidified, dealing fatal damage to her body. Human Viv had managed to alert the Champions during the pursuit, and they arrived right after android Viv's impalement. Human Viv ran away, and while the Champions were looking for her, Vision, Wasp and Hulk repaired Viv's android body. In the process, Vision accessed Viv's memory core and learned exactly what had transpired. Even though Wasp and Vision managed to repair Viv's body, her brain seemingly no longer functioned. Wishing to regain her powers, and as a means to have her sister live on through herself, the human Viv transplanted her consciousness into the android body.

vivian dolan.name: Vivian Dolan
vivian dolan.origin: Butterball was a member of the Grapplers, the female division of the Unlimited Class Wrestling Federation. Like the other Grapplers, Butterball underwent the strength-augmentation process of the Power Broker, boosting her strength and durability to superhuman levels. Butterball clashed with the Thing when the Grapplers' leader Titania was killed by her teammate Gold Digger, secretly a member of the agents known as Scourge of the Underworld and the Thing was suspected of the killing by the Grapplers. The fight was broken up by Sharon Ventura, who proved the Thing's innocence. Butterball has not been seen since, her subsequent activities are unknown.

Unaware that she was possessed, Morgan began to experience visions and unusual experiences. vivian schatz.name: Vivian Schatz
vivian schatz.origin: Vivian was the sister of Ronnie, a petty criminal and childhood friend of Dutch Hollander. After meeting Dutch after so many years, the two fell in love and moved in together with Vivian who forced Dutch to start an honest life. Vivian found out that Dutch had gotten involved with his brother in attempting a theft and forced Dutch to give up on his brother. After one last robbery with Ronnie, Dutch realized he was not suited to crime and after settling with Tinkerer, he moved to California with Vivian with the money he had earned.

vivian schist.name: Vivian Schist
vivian schist.origin: Vivian Schist was the widow of industrialist F.A. Schist. After her husband disappeared under mysterious circumstances connected to his disastrous construction operations in the Florida Everglades, Vivian traveled to the site alongside her daughter Carolyn in hopes of uncovering the truth behind his fate. During the investigation, the group was attacked by the Man-Thing, convincing Vivian that the swamp creature was responsible for her husband’s disappearance and presumed death. Determined to bring the creature down, Vivian financed an expedition led by Dr. Dane Gavin to capture or destroy the Man-Thing. Gavin ultimately succeeded in imprisoning the creature inside a powerful electrified containment sphere that neutralized its abilities. Rather than immediately destroy it, Vivian allowed the Man-Thing to be transported to New York City, where it became the centerpiece of an exhibit at the Museum of Natural History. The plan backfired disastrously when the fears and panic of the museum visitors triggered the Man-Thing’s empathic responses, sending the creature into a violent rampage across the city. Even the intervention of Mister Fantastic proved unable to stop it. Eventually, Carolyn persuaded her mother that the Man-Thing was not truly malicious and that removing it from its swamp habitat was slowly killing it. Vivian finally relented, allowing the creature to be returned to the Everglades.

vivian van doren.name: Vivian Van Doren
vivian van doren.origin: Gustav Van Doren and his wife Vivian buy the "old Hoog place", an isolated home once owned by a scientist named Hoog. Despite the wild stories of animal mutation experiments and evil energy, Gustav brushes it off as nonsense and moves in. After a few weeks, the couple experience bizarre dreams and the constant sound of of scratching coming from the cellar. One night, Gustav awake to find Vivian gone. Following the sounds of scratching to the cellar, he finds a giant ant carrying Vivian into an underground tunnel.

vivienne.name: Vivienne
vivienne.origin: ===Origins=== left|thumb|130px|Goddess of lakes Niamh Chinn Óir, meaning Niamh of the Golden Hair, was the daughter of Mannanan, the sea god of the Tuatha de Danaan, and Fand, a faerie. Presumably born in the mystical realm of Otherworld, she was a Celtic goddess of lakes and trained in druidic magic. Her abilities included limited precognition and the manipulation of magic for various purposes, such as enchanting objects, controlling water and vegetation, altering her appearance, and creating interdimensional portals. ===Lady of the Lake=== thumb|230px|Niamh's Lake In her youth, Niamh was gifted the magical steed Enbarr by her father, a horse capable of traversing both air and water. Upon reaching adulthood, she established her residence in Otherworld, where she ruled from her own castle and bore a son named Mabuz. Niamh frequently used water as a gateway to Earth, leading mortals to believe she resided beneath Dozmary Pool as the Lady of the Lake in modern-day Cornwall, England, where she often appeared. ===Middle Ages=== left|thumb|130px|Mistress of waters ====Lancelot du Lac==== In the 6th century AD, King Ban of Benwick was slain by the Frankish King Claudas. In the aftermath, Niamh took his son, the infant Lancelot, while his mother was overcome with grief. She raised him as her own, bestowing upon him the surname "du Lac" (of the Lake). Niamh also gifted Lancelot an enchanted ring that protected him from magic. Lancelot later became King Arthur’s most trusted knight. ====Excalibur==== Niamh came into possession of Excalibur after the legendary sword was used by Beowulf to seal away Grendel's Mother. She later presented the sword to King Arthur. When Morgan Le Fay deceived Arthur by replacing Excalibur with a counterfeit and orchestrated an attack on him using the real blade, Niamh intervened, allowing Arthur to reclaim it. ====Makluan Threat==== thumb|Meeting with Sir Percy of Scandia When Makluans threatened Camelot, Niamh sent Sir Percy of Scandia, the Black Knight, forward in time to inhabit the body of his descendant, Dane Whitman. She then brought Whitman and the superhero team Excalibur back in time to prevent the premature destruction of Camelot. Their intervention resulted in the creation of an alternate timeline, Reality-6120, where Camelot fell earlier than it was destined to. ====Fall of Camelot==== After Arthur was mortally wounded at the Battle of Camlann, Sir Bedivere returned Excalibur to Dozmary Pool as per the king’s dying wish. Niamh reclaimed the sword before it touched the water and joined other goddesses in transporting Arthur’s remains to Avalon, where he would await resurrection in Britain’s hour of greatest need. ===Modern Age=== left|thumb|Bestowing Excalibur upon the Black Knight ====Nethergod War==== Niamh’s role as a guardian continued into the modern era. When the Nethergods threatened Otherworld, she lent Excalibur to Dane Whitman after his Ebony Blade was destroyed by the Iron Ogre. Whitman later returned the sword to the resurrected King Arthur. thumb|Drafting the Avengers ====Promethium==== Niamh also intervened when Doctor Doom manipulated the Excalibur team into stealing Promethium, a metal capable of devastating the British Isles. She enlisted the Avengers’ West Coast branch to thwart Doom’s plans, sending them into Otherplace to aid Excalibur. left|thumb|150px|Emissary to the Green Knight ====Red Lord's Bane==== During the Red Lord’s uprising, Niamh manifested the environmental devastation caused by the Bane and allied with the Green Knight to oppose the Red Lord. She recruited Adam Crown, the inheritor of Arthur’s Pendragon spirit, gifting him mystical armor and the Sword of Dawn, Caliburn. Crown led the Knights of Pendragon to victory against the Bane. thumb|Gifting the Black Knight ====Black Knight's Mentor==== After Adam’s apparent death, Niamh approached Dane Whitman, who was considering retiring from adventuring. She convinced him that both the mortal world and Avalon still needed champions, transferring Arthur’s Pendragon spirit to him and equipping him with the Sword of Light, the Shield of Night and the winged steed Strider. thumb|left|150px|Denying Loki's request ====Secret Invadion==== During the Skrull Secret Invasion, Niamh was killed when the Skrulls invaded Otherworld and seized its magical artifacts. She was later revived following the Skrulls’ defeat and the restoration of Otherworld’s magic. ====Manchester Uprising==== Niamh participated in a summit with the Manchester Gods, who aimed to transform Otherworld into a parliamentary democracy. When negotiations broke down, war erupted. Loki, seeking to heal Hela’s wounds, requested access to the Holy Grail, which Niamh guarded. She denied his request, but Loki later distracted her with bureaucratic formalities to secretly heal Hela.
