wanda zatara.species: Metamutant ( and Scarlet Witch were combined in a Marvel versus DC crossover)
wanda zatara.origin: One of Doctor Strangefate's aides, Wanda Zatara uses her metamutant-based mystical energies to atone for the misdeeds of her father. Many men fell victim to her combination of magic and seduction. Doctor Strangefate, fearing that Access (Axel Asher) would divide the Amalgam Universe into its original two universes, decided to capture and exterminate him. He had his servant Myx mystically teleport his three agents into his Sanctum, Arkham Tower: Jade Nova, Skulk, and the White Witch. When Jade Nova learned that the three of them were to capture a single man, she was annoyed, claiming that she could complete the mission alone. The White Witch essentially agreed, but she suggested herself as the only agent needed. Strangefate proceeded to explain that Access was a greater threat than any of their previous foes, including Mephisatanus or Baron Wotan. Viewing a mystically generated image of Access, the Witch thought he looked like a sweet boy. When Myx teleported the other agents away, the Witch had time to reassure her master that they would get his man. Access managed to escape Skulk and Jade Nova by teleporting, but Witch approached him from behind, pushed him on the ground, and climbed on top of him. With a kiss, she knocked him out. An amused Witch quipped that one shouldn't send a girl (Jade Nova) and a monster (Skulk) to do a woman's job. The Witch delivered the unconscious Access to the Tower of Strangefate. She explained that the other two agents were probably still looking for him. She asked for a reward, but Strangefate offered none to her. He asked her to revive Access and she did so. Strangefate asked Myx to escort her out. On the way out she flirted with Myx, asking him if he was free or busy for the night.

fields.notes: The White Witch is an amalgamation of both Scarlet Witch and DC Comics' . The White Witch is a flirtatious character who physically touches both Doctor Strangefate and Access. She also flirted with Myx. The exact origin of the powers of the White Witch is unknown. She is partly based on Zatanna, who is not completely human. Zatanna is a member of the , a sub-race of humanity with hereditary magical powers. Several other magic users of DC Comics are either full-blooded Homo Magi or hybrid descendants of them. Wanda Maximoff is, of course, a mutant. The mysterious father of the White Witch may hint at the multiple fathers of the Scarlet Witch. The parentage of Zatanna is more clear as she is a legacy character, daughter and heiress of Golden Age magical hero . While not stated as a source for this character, there is a DC character also called the White Witch. She is , an alien member of the with magical powers of her own. The White Witch somewhat resembles the , a white-haired sorceress of the Justice League. The Sorceress was created as a homage to Marvel's Scarlet Witch. Besides connections and resemblances to other comic book characters, the White Witch shares an alias with a famous literary character. The White Witch is the alternate name of Jadis, a major villain from two books in the series "The Chronicles of Narnia" by C.S. Lewis. Jadis is an extraordinarily tall and beautiful woman who uses her looks as a weapon. While the white motif in the costume of the White Witch probably derives from the uniform of Mysa Nal, the "blatantly sexual" nature of the character and the rather skimpy nature of the outfit do not. Some websites about the Amalgam characters point a resemblance of these elements to those of another Marvel character: the White Queen. The White Witch is a magical disciple and potential love interest to the otherwise cold-hearted Doctor Strangefate. Some websites about the Amalgam characters suggest that she may be his version of Clea, Dr. Strange's disciple, lover, and later wife.

wanderer government agent.name: Wanderer (Government Agent)
wanderer government agent.origin: The true identity of the US government agent known as the Wanderer remains a mystery. He works for an organization known as the Agency, though he was offered employment by a breakaway group known as Next Wave. Wanderer worked with a man called Carl Blake, who was turned into a vampire and went by the name the Night Terror. They were close friends and the men made a blood oath so that they would defend each as if they were brothers. The two came into conflict when Night Terror, as a vampire started killing former government employees, so the Wanderer was sent to track him down and capture him alive. He tracked down Night Terror when he was attacking some off duty agents and rescued as many as he could. He fought Night Terror as best he could, but lost and had his blood drank, but survived. Night Terror tried to attack again but some of his memories were restored. Night Terror left his old friend for dead, but somehow, Wanderer survived with no ill effects or vampiric change.

wanderer mutant.name: Wanderer (Mutant)
wanderer mutant.origin: Wanderer was a slaver. She was an associate of Sanguine, Beldame, and Goth. When Havok joined forces with Emma Frost, Bastion, and Miss Sinister to release the power-bestowing Mothervine virus on a global scale, Wanderer was one of the many mutants at the service of this cabal. She helped carry out an attack against Magneto's X-Men to stop them from interfering with Havok's plans. After the villains were defeated, Bloodstorm used her vampiric hypnosis to make the Wanderer teleport them to Havok's hideout.

wanxia.name: Wanxia
wanxia.origin: Raised separate from her brother Zaoxing in a Taiji lab and told he was stillborn, Wanxia grew up unable to control her ability to generate intense cold, with her only interaction being the occasional visit from her caretaker, Bao. Withdrawn, but intelligent, she always felt like she could feel a presence just beyond her reach. At some point prior to the age of 16, she and her brother finally exerted enough control over their powers to reach for that vague feeling both felt. Meeting for the first time, they found that when they touched, their powers were explosive and unmatched. Traveling to New York City at the age of 16, the duo helped the Avengers fight robots developed by A.I.M., and informed them of the threat posed by Taiji.

war first horsemen.name: War (First Horsemen)
war first horsemen.origin: ===Origins=== War was one of four children born to Apocalypse and Genesis, the mutant leaders of Okkara. The four grew up to become the first iteration of their father's Horsemen. They were raised in Okkara, although they did briefly leave Okkara to fight the Brood in 2620 BC, Egypt, alongside the Brotherhood of the Shield's founder, Imhotep. When their homeland of Okkara was attacked by Annihilation and its hordes of Amenthi daemons, War and the rest of her people fought to defend their sacred land. Eventually, it became clear that the mutants could not win. Okkara was split into two halves, and it was decided that the entire mutant society would be sealed away into the alien world of Amenth, to buy Apocalypse time to prepare mutantkind for the daemons' inevitable return. ===Arakko=== On the half of Okkara that would eventually become known as Arakko, the mutants created a series of towers to protect them against the daemons. War, her siblings and the other mutants fought for millennia in an endless war, as generations of mutants lived and died within the safety of the towers. War married a mutant by the name of Bracken, and the two had a child who would become known as Summoner. Bracken was killed in a duel by the mutant Solem. The reasons for the duel are unknown, though it is speculated either that the two were lovers or that Solem killed him to upset War, who had long refused his advances. In either case, War had Solem imprisoned in an isolated cell, giving him Bracken's dagger in the hope that he would eventually kill himself with it after the despair and loneliness grew too much. Eventually, War's mother Genesis, accepted a duel against Annihilation, for the fate of their two peoples. Genesis won, but it proved a hollow victory, as without a host, the daemonic children of Annihilation would go on an uncontrollable rampage, dooming the Arakki, leaving Genesis with the choice to merge with the entity and fall under its control, or stand idly by as her home was destroyed. When the desperate Arakkii opened a portal to Dryador, Genesis merged with Annihilation, hoping to control it, only to fall under its sway. She led the armies of Amenth to the conquest of Arakko. The mutants were subjugated, and War and her siblings were now forced to lead the armies of their lifelong enemies. ===X of Swords=== With Arakko subjugated, Annihilation prepared for the invasion of Earth. War's son, Summoner, would be sent with a piece of Arakko to Earth in order to manipulate his grandfather into opening a portal to allow the Amenthi forces to reach Earth, while War and the Horsemen would lead the armies of Amenth to the conquest of Dryador. After the fall of Dryador, the Horsemen laid siege to the Starlight Citadel, the very nexus of Otherworld. During the siege, they were reunited with their father, who had been led there by Summoner, together with a squadron of Krakoan mutants. They ambushed him, mortally wounding him before he was extracted by the Krakoans. As the Horsemen and their armies battled the Krakoans, Opal Luna Saturnyne, Omniversal Majestrix and ruler of Otherworld, interrupted the conflict. She managed to produce a truce between the combatants, and offered to host a tournament to settle the matter; the Horsemen and their armies would depart, but return in a few days time to fight the champions of Otherworld; the mutants of Krakoa, for the right to cross Otherworld into Earth. Saturnyne produced a prophecy, bidding each side to produce ten specific sword-bearers wielding specific swords. War and her brother Death were two of the chosen sword-bearers. The Horsemen set about finding the swords and their wielders. War and Pestilence recruited the mercenary Pogg Ur-Pogg and their aunt Isca the Unbeaten to their cause. To War's dismay, one of the chosen sword-bearers was none other than Solem. War was enraged to find him in good spirits, as the citizens or Arakko had taken care of him during his imprisonment. She reluctantly released him so that he could find his sword. With their sword-bearers found, they traveled to Otherworld to begin the tournament. Before the tournament, Saturnyne arranged a banquet to allow the contestants to mingle. In order to secure victory for Arakko, War poisoned Krakoan mutant Wolverine's food, believing he would be their great impediment in the tournament. The food was instead eaten by Cypher, who was rescued from choking to death by the Arakkii sword-bearer White Sword, who dismissed War's actions as cowardice. War's first challenge was to face her "teammate" Solem in a duel to see who could sever the opponent's limb first. However, Solem was allowed to call in a favor he was owed by Wolverine, allowing him to fight in his place. war zone robot.name: War Zone (Robot)
war zone robot.origin: While in her apartment, the Sensational She-Hulk was attacked by the War Zone robot, and during the fight, it sprayed her with a gas that appeared to have no effect, before being destroyed. This gas was later revealed upon analysis by Reed Richards to contain a toxin that neutralised the Sensational She-Hulk’s powers. Later, during the Sensational She-Hulk's guest appearance on Heartbreak Hospital, a rebuilt War Zone attacked again. The two fought, and it was heavily damaged when it fell into a pool and short circuited. It recovered and set itself to self-destruct, but it was destroyed prematurely when Zapper absorbed its energy with a neutralizing suit.

warbot.name: Warbot
warbot.origin: The Warbot is a model of robot warrior with insectoid features designed and built by A.I.M. An early Warbot was taken by a team of A.I.M. agents with them when they attacked Doctor Strange’s mansion, then the de facto headquarters of the Defenders. The robot proved very effective, fighting the Hulk, and either proving resistant to or deflecting the attacks of two magical Defenders, Clea and the Valkyrie. Trapping the Hulk in a chunk of crystal that rendered him unconscious, the Warbot left with the green giant, unaware the Defender Nighthawk had attached a tracking transmitter to the A.I.M. ship. The ship reached an A.I.M. laboratory at Long Island, where the attack team was surprised by Nighthawk along with Ms. Marvel and Hellcat, and a new fight started. Ms. Marvel attacked the Warbot, proving more effective than the others, smashing its part and weapons one at a time. She damaged it enough finally that she threw it into the emptied lab where it exploded, destroying the A.I.M. base. Years later, another Warbot (possibly the first refurbished) attended a mecha rave party aboard a sunken German U-boat on the bottom of the ocean. Also in attendance were Gothic Lolita, Social Butterfly, and an undercover Iron Man. The Warbot wore a piece of “bling” in the shape of a woman’s torso around its neck.

warbow crystalium.name: Warbow (Crystalium)
warbow crystalium.first_appearance: Saga of Crystar, Crystal Warrior Vol 1 1
warbow crystalium.origin: Warbow was a Crystal Warrior from the Crystalium kingdom and a close friend of his king Crystar. After the crystal kingdom ended in the bizare domain known as Weirdworld, Warbow appeared to be the sole survivor of Crystalium after Morgan Le Fay destroyed that. The warrior was captured by the Underwater Apes, but he could easily escaped from his prison, even if he was never able to reach the surface again until Arkon the Magnificent was captured as well; the duo was able to break free from the Apes and to return to the surface. There, they allied to break into Morgan Le Fay's castle in order to get back the pieces of Crystar, so that Warbow could use those to rebuild his king. Once rebuilt the whole kingdom, Warbow continued fighting against everyone who oppressed the weakest in Weirdworld such as the Master of Weirdworld.

warbringer.name: Warbringer
warbringer.origin: The Chitauri known as Warbringer was an excessively cruel warlord who was kept in hibernation until his violent methods were deemed appropriate. He was awakened to take revenge on Nova for stealing millions from the Chitauri Reserve Bank, and recover a warship and the escaped gladiators (among them Nova's missing father) who had stolen it. thumb|left During the transaction with a bounty hunter for the location of the stolen warship, Warbringer used his ship's tractor beam to pick and fire hundreds of asteroids at Earth at a velocity that would ensure an extinction-level event just to get Nova's attention. Later, upon approaching the stolen warship, Warbringer engaged Nova in a brief fight in which he revealed he had redirected asteroids towards Earth, leaving with no other choice other than leave to protect his planet. In the meantime, Warbringer captured the escaped gladiators and recovered the warship. After setting course to Earth so he could finish his job, Warbringer was attacked again by Nova, who had left Earth under the care of his superhuman friends. Nova tried to force Warbringer into surrendering by flying with him into the Sun, but ended up losing him inside the star when his arm was burned off his body. He was eventually rescued by his crew after they surrendered to Nova and released their prisoners. ===Battling the Avengers=== Teleporting to Earth through on-the-spot cloning and thought transference, Warbringer found himself in what used to be the Avengers Tower. Its new owner, the nefarious CEO of Qeng Enterprises, Mister Gryphon, recognized Warbringer's language and tried to become his ally. The mysterious man offered the Warbringer the chance to destroy humanity and be remembered as a galactic legend, and the only thing he had to do was to assemble three pieces of an ancient artifact left on Earth by a Chitauri millenia ago and use it. As the CEO showed what such artifact was capable of, they noticed the presence of Spider-Man eavesdropping. The unwanted guest was blasted through a wall, which caught the attention of Iron Man and Captain America, who proceeded to confront Warbringer brief moments after the CEO teleported away. Warbringer knocked out the three heroes with an energy blast, and proclaimed the Earth would be his. thumb|right Warbringer went to the Liberty Science Center, in New Jersey, and took the first piece of the Chitauri artifact, which was in display there. He was confronted by Ms. Marvel and his nemesis Nova, but he created a distraction by setting the neighbor buildings on fire and escaped. Later, Warbringer was confronted by the heroes he fought earlier and the Vision at the PATH Station on Grove, where he found the second piece of the artifact buried in its walls. Afterwards, he was attacked by Thor, but her hammer was teleported away by Gryphon before it could hit Warbringer and ended up destroying the underwater tunnel's wall. As the tunnel was flooded by the water, Warbringer left the heroes behind to find the third and final piece of the artifact. The final segment of the artifact was found in a Hart Island graveyard. As soon as the pieces were connected, a portal was summoned in the sky, with a massive Chitauri army ready to come through. However, the heroes that were on his trail quickly caught up with Warbringer and gathered the pieces together. While Vision, Thor and Nova tried to defeat Warbringer, Iron Man realized that if the pieces came together once again, the summoned portal would open, so he planned to have the pieces connected, force Warbringer through the portal, and destroy the artifact to close the portal. After Iron Man's failed attempt to execute the plan, Nova tackled the villain and managed to force him through the portal. Warbringer was returned to his homeworld through the portal, but he found he had also been transported to the future. He appeared before a group of Chitauri soldiers, who recognized his uniform from childhood lessons. Warbringer panicked after realizing his predicament, and the Chitauri soldiers seemingly killed him for his insolence. ===Infinity Countdown=== Somehow returned to life and his own timeline, Warbringer captured the criminal Talinda and offered her her life in exchange for the location of the Power Stone, which he would use to liberate his homeworld from Thanos. Warbringer subsequently led a fleet of Chitauri soldiers into attacking Xitaung, the planet where the Power Stone had manifested in a giant size. Its protectors, the Nova Corps were already fending off against invaders, the Fraternity of Raptors. Once the Chitauri managed to overpower their enemies, both the Raptors and the Nova Corps decided to retreat. The Nova's allies, the Guardians of the Galaxy, held the line for them. After Star-Lord managed to reduce the Power Stone to a manageable size, he passed it to Drax the Destroyer, who used it to repel the Chitauri. Without the Power Stone serving as its anchor, Xitaung was plunged into the star it orbited

ward meachum.name: Ward Meachum
ward meachum.origin: ===Early Life=== Ward Meachum was a successful businessman and the brother of Harold Meachum, CEO of Rand-Meachum Inc. ===Iron Fist=== Harold Meachum killed his business partner Wendell Rand, Daniel Rand's father. When Daniel Rand, as Iron Fist, returned from K'un-Lun to New York City years later to seek his revenge against Harold, he could not kill him. However, the Ninja silently killed Harold and the murder was pinned on Iron Fist. Ward hired Batroc the Leaper to kill the Iron Fist, but he failed. Ward, with Harold's daughter Joy, sought revenge against the Iron Fist. Ward hired villains and developed elaborate schemes to kill the Iron Fist. ===Steel Serpent=== Ward hired Steel Serpent to help them take revenge on Iron Fist. They watched the battle between Iron Fist and Radion on television, hoping he would survive so they could get their revenge. Danny tried to regain control of the business from the Meachums. Ward had several dealings with criminals that would come back to haunt him, for example with the Golden Tiger Gang led by Chaka Khan. Steel Serpent came to Ward to tell him he would no longer work for him due to his criminal connections, beating his bodyguards and leaving Ward alone. Steel Serpent vowed that with his debt to Joy Meachum paid, he would simply get his revenge on Iron Fist. ===Heroes for Hire=== Ward Meachum began to work for Master Khan. He hired a group of men to steal the Power Gem of Quon back from Danny Rand. Alongside the men was Fera, a lupine humanoid who disliked Meachum, only loyal to Master Khan. Ward hired Shades and Comanche and decked them both out with new weapons, Shades with a pair of optic blasting shades, and Comanche with trick arrows. He sent them against Iron Fist and Luke Cage. They knocked him out before leaving and telling the bystanders to tell Cage that they have a score to settle when he revived. Cage tracked them down to the George Washington Bridge, where Cage and Iron Fist learned the truth about their employer. While in hiding, Ward spotted D.W. filming the fight between Shades and Comanche and worried that he was caught on tape to be implicated in his plot against the two heroes, and vowed to get the film before it could be reviewed. Cage and Iron Fist managed to easily defeat Shades and Comanche, however when the police took the two away, they failed to remove Shade's visor, and he managed to fire one final blast, hitting the heroes and knocking them off the bridge. Ward and his men used the Power Gem of Quon on a special pedestal to summon Master Khan back to the Earth dimension. Master Khan told Meachum that the Power Gem was leeching away the power of Shou-Lao from Iron Fist, a process that would give him the dragon's power and kill his eternal foe. They were attacked by the Heroes for Hire, and Master Khan was forced to fight Iron Fist. During the fight the crystal was destroyed, sending Master Khan back to K'un-Lun. Following the battle, Meachum and his men were all arrested. ===Super-Skrull=== In time Joy learned the truth about her father's death, and began working with Danny again, becoming partners at the Rand Corporation. Ward still hated Rand, and agreed to help Kl'rt, the Super-Skrull with his conquest of Earth in exchange for the hand of the "most beautiful woman in the Skrull Galaxy". However Phoebe Marrs of Oracle Inc. and friend to Namor told Meachum that beautiful by Skrull standards would be horrific by human standards. Due to Meachum's paranoia, Ward betrayed the Skrulls and tried to destroy their machine. Super-Skrull had no choice but to incinerate Meachum on the spot. Unbeknownst to Meachum, Kl'rt kept his word and had convinced the beautiful Lady Tenelle to marry Ward as part of their deal.
ward meachum.bio: ===Early Life=== Ward Meachum was a successful businessman and the brother of Harold Meachum, CEO of Rand-Meachum Inc. ===Iron Fist=== Harold Meachum killed his business partner Wendell Rand, Daniel Rand's father. When Daniel Rand, as Iron Fist, returned from K'un-Lun to New York City years later to seek his revenge against Harold, he could not kill him. However, the Ninja silently killed Harold and the murder was pinned on Iron Fist. Ward hired Batroc the Leaper to kill the Iron Fist, but he failed. Ward, with Harold's daughter Joy, sought revenge against the Iron Fist. Ward hired villains and developed elaborate schemes to kill the Iron Fist. ===Steel Serpent=== Ward hired Steel Serpent to help them take revenge on Iron Fist. They watched the battle between Iron Fist and Radion on television, hoping he would survive so they could get their revenge. Danny tried to regain control of the business from the Meachums. Ward had several dealings with criminals that would come back to haunt him, for example with the Golden Tiger Gang led by Chaka Khan. Steel Serpent came to Ward to tell him he would no longer work for him due to his criminal connections, beating his bodyguards and leaving Ward alone. Steel Serpent vowed that with his debt to Joy Meachum paid, he would simply get his revenge on Iron Fist. ===Heroes for Hire=== Ward Meachum began to work for Master Khan. He hired a group of men to steal the Power Gem of Quon back from Danny Rand. Alongside the men was Fera, a lupine humanoid who disliked Meachum, only loyal to Master Khan. Ward hired Shades and Comanche and decked them both out with new weapons, Shades with a pair of optic blasting shades, and Comanche with trick arrows. He sent them against Iron Fist and Luke Cage. They knocked him out before leaving and telling the bystanders to tell Cage that they have a score to settle when he revived. Cage tracked them down to the George Washington Bridge, where Cage and Iron Fist learned the truth about their employer. While in hiding, Ward spotted D.W. filming the fight between Shades and Comanche and worried that he was caught on tape to be implicated in his plot against the two heroes, and vowed to get the film before it could be reviewed. Cage and Iron Fist managed to easily defeat Shades and Comanche, however when the police took the two away, they failed to remove Shade's visor, and he managed to fire one final blast, hitting the heroes and knocking them off the bridge. Ward and his men used the Power Gem of Quon on a special pedestal to summon Master Khan back to the Earth dimension. Master Khan told Meachum that the Power Gem was leeching away the power of Shou-Lao from Iron Fist, a process that would give him the dragon's power and kill his eternal foe. They were attacked by the Heroes for Hire, and Master Khan was forced to fight Iron Fist. During the fight the crystal was destroyed, sending Master Khan back to K'un-Lun. Following the battle, Meachum and his men were all arrested. ===Super-Skrull=== In time Joy learned the truth about her father's death, and began working with Danny again, becoming partners at the Rand Corporation. Ward still hated Rand, and agreed to help Kl'rt, the Super-Skrull with his conquest of Earth in exchange for the hand of the "most beautiful woman in the Skrull Galaxy". However Phoebe Marrs of Oracle Inc. and friend to Namor told Meachum that beautiful by Skrull standards would be horrific by human standards. Due to Meachum's paranoia, Ward betrayed the Skrulls and tried to destroy their machine. Super-Skrull had no choice but to incinerate Meachum on the spot. Unbeknownst to Meachum, Kl'rt kept his word and had convinced the beautiful Lady Tenelle to marry Ward as part of their deal.

ward strongbow.name: Ward Strongbow
ward strongbow.origin: Ward Strongbow was Navajo and the brother of Jason Strongbow, the man who would become "American Eagle". At some point Ward was sent to a university off the reservation where he seemed to gain a dislike for both Native American and White Culture. Ward returned to the tribe and assisted Jason lead it but unbeknownst to Jason, Ward allied with a mining company, ran by Klaw and allowed them to set up on operation on their reservation to secretly mine uranium. Jason attempted to stop the operation through the courts but they rejected his initial attempts and Jason felt a follow-up was taking too long so lead a protest against the miners. A protestor was accidentally shot and Jason followed the shooter into the mines where he discovered Ward and the uranium mining equipment. The pair fought and Jason's torch accidentally set the machinery on fire and then Klaw arrived and blasted Jason into the machinery. The equipment exploded and the radiation combined with Klaw's sonics gave both Jason and Ward powers. Ward was then carried away by Klaw's men and Jason believed he was kidnapped. Travelling to the Savage Land, Ward then assisted Klaw in mining operations there to extract Vibranium. Jason (now as American Eagle) arrived with Ka-Zar, Thing, and Wyatt Wingfoot and discovered Ward was allied with Klaw. Ward and Jason fought though they were equally matched. Klaw's men however, believed Ward was loosing and fired on the pair but accidentally hit and killed Ward. After the men were defeated Jason picked his brother's body to return back to their reservation.

warden cashman.name: Warden Cashman
warden cashman.origin: Cashman was the Warden of the Robert Kelly Correctional Facility aka The Box which was specially created to imprison mutants. After members of the X-Men were incarcerated at the Box, they were sentenced to three days of solitary confinement by Cashman after a fight broke out between the X-Men and a gang led by Crazy Maisie. After an attack by the Negative Zone god Scythian in the city of Paris, Magik paid a visit to Warden Cashman in his office to see if he would release her fellow teammates since they were the ones who had experience battling this monster. Cashman denied her request but Storm who released herself from confinement threatened Cashman to let them go or he would suffer the consequences.

wardog.name: Wardog
wardog.origin: Wardog was the leader of the Special Executive. He is known to have lost his left arm in a conflict with the . Wardog was hired by Saturnyne to recruit Captain Britain to testify for her when she was put on trial by the Dimensional Development Court. At Saturnyne's trial, Captain Britain became angry and attacked the Dimensional Development Court following Mandragon's destruction of Earth-238 and Saturnyne's death sentence. Wardog and the rest of the Executive helped Captain Britain and Saturnyne escape. They fled to Earth-616 and took up temporary residence in Braddock manor. When the Fury attacked Captain UK outside Braddock Manor, the Special Executive got involved in the battle. The Special Executive began to take casualties. Although the Special Executive helped to temporarily cripple the creature, the Fury managed to escaped. Wardog left Earth with the surviving members of the Special Executive.

warhead construct.origin: The Warhead was a massive weapon inspired form the mind of Andrew "Slugger" Johnson, an aficionado of the 1950s who had reality altered for him by the Shaper of Worlds. warlock.name: Warlock
warlock.origin: ===Early Life=== The alien being called Warlock came from a Kvch in an unspecified location in outer space. Warlock's race was a sentient form of "techno-organic" life known as the Technarchy, which resembled circuitry and machinery in various ways. Members of this race gave birth to great numbers of offspring, who resided in a "creche," although the process of birth may have been very different for this race than it was for life forms native to Earth. Children of this race proved their right to exist by battling their parents to the death; either the child killed the parent, or the parent slew the child. Warlock was the son of the Magus, the ruler of his native world and apparently its most powerful being. Warlock recognized his mutation when he realized that he did not care to slay his father. This change in idealism marked Warlock a mutant in his race. Fearful of being slain in combat by the Magus, Warlock fled his native planet but was pursued through outer space by the Magus himself. ===Coming to Earth=== Warlock found himself approaching Earth. Attracted by unusual energy sources, Warlock first crashed through Asteroid M, the base of the superhuman mutant, Magneto, destroying it. He finally landed on Earth near Professor Charles Xavier's mansion, which held various alien Shi'ar technology, sensing the artificial intelligence of the mansion's Shi'ar computers. ===New Mutants=== Prof. Xavier's mansion was the home and headquarters of two teams of superhuman mutants, the New Mutants and the X-Men. Disoriented by his new surroundings and terribly frightened, Warlock clashed with the New Mutants, who at first regarded him as a threat. Warlock's life energies ebbed so much that the despairing young alien lay near death. The New Mutants summoned their friend Doug Ramsey, who succeeded in initiating communication with Warlock, and the New Mutants befriended the alien. With Professor Xavier's permission, Warlock joined their group. Ramsey also became a member of the New Mutants as Cypher. Warlock had a personality greatly resembling in part that of a young child, but nevertheless proved to be a valuable member of the New Mutants and a worthy ally of the X-Men. Warlock remained beside his friends throughout his time on Earth. A recurring problem among Warlock and his friends, Dani Moonstar especially, was that Warlock needed to assimilate and drain the "life glow" of an organic being to sustain his life. When appearing in public, Warlock used his powers to assume a human appearance. Later, Amora the Enchantress kidnapped the New Mutants to Asgard. Warlock found himself in Hel, Hela's realm, and she simply allowed him to leave stating that he didn't even know his potential. There, Warlock first began forming around Doug to become a suit of armor to protect Doug. After their adventure in Asgard, the New Mutants found themselves under the guidance of a new teacher, Magneto. Warlock found himself capable of merging physically and mentally with Doug, so that they could operate as a gestalt. This developed a danger of permanently infecting Ramsey with the Transmode Virus and permanently merging the two so that they would not want to revert to normalcy. Not long after this adventure, Warlock and the other NMs came to the X-Men's aid when Mojo de-aged said team to infancy and mind controlled them. During the battle that followed, the New Mutants succeeded in freeing the X-Men from Mojo's control. When the Magus confronted the New Mutants, Magik teleported her team away to Limbo and the Magus followed them. Magus allied himself with the demon, S'ym and infected many of Limbo's other denizens with the Transmode Virus. When merging their forms once more, Cypher tapped into Warlock's own DNA in order to learn how to "re-code" it. While the rest of the New Mutants distracted Magus, Cypher and Warlock re-wrote the Magus' DNA, effectively reducing him to infancy. Upon returning home, the Impossible Man arrived to "have fun" with the X-Men. With the X-Men nowhere to be found, Impossible Man and Warlock engaged in a contest of shape-shifting and teleported around the world. The New Mutants were forced to chase Warlock and Impossible Man, until Warlock won the contest, due to the fact that he was able to change color as well. ===Fallen Angels=== A friendly soccer game went wrong when Sunspot accidentally gave Cannonball a concussion and, after fearing himself to be a danger to his team, ran away. Warlock believed that the team needed to be whole in order to effectively operate and went after Sunspot. Warlock arrived in time to rescue Bobby Da Costa from a group of thugs, after Bobby's solar power had expired, and suggested that they stick together, after Bobby stated that he was not worthy to return to the New Mutants. After the pair attempted to rob a church, they were found by a duplicate of Jamie Madrox (attempting to return them to the New Mutants) and Gomi (propositioning Bobby to join the Fallen Angels). warlord sakaar.name: Warlord (Sakaar)
warlord sakaar.origin: Before the fall of the Red King, the man that would become known as the Warlord was a Sakaaran criminal locked for life in the darkest prison of Crown City. When the capital exploded, the Warlord found himself free. Over time, he proceeded to conquer over a hundred tribes from Sakaar, uniting them into a single dominant faction. He regularly forced slaves and minor clans to battle for survival in a barbaric trial known as the Gauntlet. The Doka'abi became the first clan to make it past the Gauntlet's first round due to their members having sought the Hulk's help to fight on their behalf as their champion. Angered by the Hulk's victory, the Warlord demanded Lickspit to find how the Doka'abi opened the Great Portal, where the Hulk had came through, in order to fight somebody as strong as the Hulk to fight against him. After the Hulk made it through the second round, the Warlord invited him to his Tower for a feast. After the Warlord shared his backstory and philosophy of life with with his guest, the Hulk threatened to kill him if he cheated the Doka'abi Clan of freedom after winning the Gauntlet. After the Hulk passed the fourth round, the Warlord announced himself as the Hulk's final opponent. In preparation for the final round, the Warlord had his slaves ready a Soviet warhead he had obtained at some point. When the final battle was being announced, the Warlord abruptly attacked the Hulk and used tracking missiles on him. The Hulk turned the Warlord's arsenal against him, and evaded the missiles until he made the remaining two hit him while jumping at the Warlord, engulfing both of them in fire. When the Hulk tried to make the Warlord surrender, he warned him he would come after the Hulk's allies unless he was killed. The Warlord then had the nuclear warhead fired from the Tower to the battlefield. After knocking out cold the Warlord, the Hulk absorbed the radiation from the explosion. While the Doka'abi were celebrating the Hulk's victory, the clan's headman Chak approached the fallen Warlord and stabbed him in the chest with a spear.

warner grant.name: Warner Grant
warner grant.origin: While attempting to cross the plains to hunt for buffalo Red Hawk and the Apache Kid are surprised to find a fence put up on part of the land and a warning from Warner Grant, the landowner, that all trespassers particularly Native Americans will be shot on sight. Faced with the potential starvation of his people, the Apache Kid tells Red Hawk and the others to wait for him to find a solution to the problem and rides off. Out of sight the Apache Kid changes into his alter-ego of Aloysius Kare and crosses over onto Grant's land. Shortly after doing so he is almost blown up by an explosive charge and shot at by Grant himself. Grant warns Kare that his land is boobytrapped with explosives and explains that he has done so to keep people off his land, Native Americans in particular due to the bloodshed caused by the last Indian War he vowed to never let either party on any land that he should own. Kare tells Grant that he has no right to bar the Apaches from getting to the hunting grounds they have used for hundreds of years. Grant refuses to listen and sets off another charge using the blast to escape. The blast also frees a flow of water that threatens to flood the gulch they are fighting in. Kare manages to escape the quickly flooding land, and tracks Grant back to his home. There he spots some of the flood water seeping toward the electrified fence that Grant has erected around his property. The sparks from the contact from the water and fence cause Grant's house to light on fire with Grant trapped inside. Kare then changes into the Apache Kid and rescues Grant from the danger. Realizing the errors of his way, Grant promises to take down his fence and allow the Apaches to travel through his land to hunt from now on.

Unfortunately for Hedy, Patsy and Buzz were unaffected after Warner left.

warren curzon.name: Warren Curzon
warren curzon.origin: Curzon was a British Detective Inspector staying at the Manhattan Ash Hotel and working detached to Code: Blue investigating psychics all having the same dream of a dying tree. After finding the bodies of men working for Prof. Price, he started to realize that Thor was involved. After studying Asgardian mythology, Curzon realized Thor's disappearance and the deaths of Price's men meant that Thor was killed by the world tree Yggdrasill. Using a device that could track the energy of Mjolnir, Curzon searched for Thor's body. However, he encountered the Enchantress who vaporized him in an instant.

warren hempstead.name: Warren Hempstead
warren hempstead.origin: Professor Hampstead was an archaeologist who with his team was carrying out excavations in Egypt but for a long time without any discoveries, until the day during the excavation they found a petrified human figure more than two thousand years old. When the petrified body was completely discovered, it came to life, revealing itself to be the Sphinx which had remained in suspended animation for millennia. He and his team were taken prisoner by the Sphinx and forced to excavate his pyramid, until he met the Thing and informed him of what was happening. During the battle between the Thing and the Sphinx, Professor Hempstead escaped, freeing his team as well.

warren miles.name: Warren Miles
warren miles.origin: Before faking his own death by having a clone of himself die at Shea Stadium, the Jackal created several clones of himself in order to make his identity immortal through their lives, with the hope that they would have a better life than him. One of these clones, after discovering himself to be such, tracked down Joyce Delaney, a clone of Gwen Stacy, and married her. He took the name of Warren Miles while she decided to go by Gwen Miles. When confronted by Peter Parker, Warren forced Gwen to go on the run with him and died after his car crashed into a river because of the all-new Green Goblin. His body melted due to clone degeneration.

warren tork.name: Warren Tork
warren tork.origin: Warren Tork was a member of Moon Knight's Shadow Cabinet under the alias "Junior Birdman". Tork seemed to be a computer hacker and conspiracy theorist who provided his own unique perspective and contacts to the Cabinet. He may have also had more violent, anarchistic leanings, as Sheriff once mentioned Tork was still wanted in California for actions taken decades ago before he went underground. Herb and Sheila Hollister, the Harlequin Hit-Man, killed him after being brainwashed by the Ghost in the Telephone.

warren traveler.name: Warren Traveler
warren traveler.origin: On Earth-58163 (the altered reality created by the Scarlet Witch of Earth-616), Sir Warren Traveler was once a Sorcerer Supreme in the service of the King of England. He greatly enhanced his power by replacing his right eye with the Eye of Watoomb (the remnant of his world's Wand of Watoomb), which he located at a magic shop in Hell's Kitchen. After acquiring the Eye, Traveler went on a rampage that was stopped by Captain Marvel (Carol Danvers), who punched him into submission. Throughout the following seven years, Traveler continually attacked Captain Marvel in order to get revenge on her to no avail, leading up to a confrontation in which she thwarted his attack by throwing a "cat" (later named Chewie) at him, thus disrupting the time-travel spell he was casting and sending him to another dimension alongside the feline alien. A month after reality had been returned to normal, Traveler returned to Earth with the cat. He attacked Ms. Marvel (Carol Danvers) in order to settle their unfinished business, but ended up losing his grip on reality and started treating her as an old friend. Confused, Ms. Marvel knocked him out and took him to Doctor Strange. Strange determined that the switching of realities had caused Traveler's mental instability and convinced Carol to leave, intending to depower Traveler before he could become a more serious problem. However, Traveler freed himself from his restraints, seized the Wand of Watoomb in Strange's possession, and attacked him with it. Strange was able to telepathically contact Ms. Marvel and she returned to the Sanctum Sanctorum to rescue him. Marvel ended up being pulled into Earth-6095, an alternate dimension where the entire population of Earth had been devoured by a swarm of alien insects. There, she was confronted by Traveler, who had regained his sanity thanks to the Wand of Watoomb he had stolen from Strange. Planning to travel across realities to access other sources of magic that could keep his mind stabilized, Traveler thanked Ms. Marvel for revealing to him the potential of alternate realities, and took her to the past of the one they were in, right to the moment the swarm of alien insects arrived on Earth. Traveler planned to leave Carol there to die, but saw himself forced to return them both to her home reality after she was able to steal the Wand from him. Traveler intentionally took them back seconds before he had started his battle against Doctor Strange in the Sanctum, taking advantage of the situation to steal the Wand back and escape to parts unknown. Ms. Marvel then joined forces with Strange to deal with Traveler's past self. He vanished soon after unleashing the magic energy that sent Carol to Earth-6095, thus closing the temporal loop he had created.

warren worthington iii.origin: ===Early Life=== thumb|left|Warren Worthington III as a child. Warren Worthington III was a member of the wealthy Worthington family, son of Warren Worthington Jr. and his wife Kathryn. Doctor Stuart who delivered him immediately spotted the distortion of his shoulder blades and guessed what he would become. On top of family wealth, Warren was an attractive boy, and seemed naturally skilled at anything he tried. In elementary school, Warren was an exemplary student, and was teased by his classmates who called him "little angel". Warren was obsessed with the sky and birds to the point where it distracted him from social gatherings, earning the ire of his father. It was in his youth that Warren was first brought to the exclusive Hellfire Club for a party. Warren's obsession with flying grew to an infatuation with heights, something that frightened his parents when Warren started climbing trees. Eventually, Warren was placed in the Fairburn Boys School where he continued to excel in his classes. It was here that he discovered women who were naturally attracted to him due to his fleet moves and dancing ability. One of his childhood friends during this period of time was Candace Southern, who secretly had a crush on Warren. Warren's first girlfriend was Cressida Desford, but he could not compete with her obsession with super-heroes and they soon drifted apart. ===Private School=== thumb|Pre-mutation bruising. Warren soon changed schools, attending St. Joes Catholic School. There he continued to excel in sports, beating the high jumping record. His friends during this period included Brandon Hardy, who was on the track team, and the meek Andrew Palmer. He was also dating cheerleader Amanda Cobb, the most popular and attractive girl in school. Warren became conceded, and scoffed at the idea that he might be using steroids to enhance his performance. When he bragged to his coach about his skills being the only thing allowing the school to win track meets, this caused tension between Warren and Brandon. It was this time that Warren's mutant abilities were being able to manifest. Physical in nature, Warren noticed that bruises were starting to spread on his back. Assuming the worst, Warren believed he was dying and tried to write a letter telling his parents to pull him out of classes, but he tore the letter up and threw it out, unaware that Andrew had recovered the scraps and pieced it together. Warren's condition got even more strange when he woke up one morning to find a feather in his bed. Things were about to take a change for Warren Worthington III, as a religious zealot was travelling the country with his prisoner - a precognitive mutant Mary-Margaret - killing mutants with powers that he saw as an affront to God. Warren's relationship with Amanda Cobb ended when she noticed that there were nubs growing from the bruises on his back. Not wanting to explain what he thought was happening, Warreb abruptly broke up with her. Jilted, Amanda then started dating Brandon Hardy. Fearing what may be happening to him, Warren began studying on birds and their molting patterns. On the night of the annual Hell Night, Warren came to aid Andrew, who was being hazed by his classmates for being a freshman. Warren knocked out Brandon and rushed Andrew to his room. There, a clearly smitten Andrew, revealed that he knew Warren's secret. Warren was later surprised when he discovered that the grows were wings that were starting to grow from his back. Warren later came to the aid of another bullied student, Cameron Hodge who began to idolize Warren. As Warren's wings began to grow in size, they became hard to conceal, and he started strapping them to his back. In order to avoid suspicion, he abruptly quit all athletics in school, much to the confusion of his coaches and administrators. When a fire broke out in his dorm at Phillips Academy in Exeter, New Hampshire, Warren decided to do something about it. Using costumes from the theater storeroom, Warren dressed up as an Angel and saved those imperiled by the fire. One of these students was Cameron Hodge, who instantly recognized Warren despite his disguise, although he kept this secret for many decades afterward. During the Christmas break, Andrew convinced Warren to stay behind instead of going home for the holidays. Warren took the opportunity to test out his new wings and their ability to make him fly. There was a near accident when he accidentally dropped Andrew in a frozen pond, but was able to revive him with CPR. It was not long after this that Warren discovered that the school priest, Father Reynolds, was secretly molesting Andrew, and Warren decided to do something about it. Using the props from the theater department again, Warren disguised himself as Michael the Archangel and tricked Father Reynolds into confessing his crimes. As Reynolds was being led away, Brandon Hardy teased Andrew, and Warren once again came to his defense. This led to a brawl that included Amanda Cobb

Warren's condition got even more strange when he woke up one morning to find a feather in his bed. Things were about to take a change for Warren Worthington III, as a religious zealot was travelling the country with his prisoner - a precognitive mutant Mary-Margaret - killing mutants with powers that he saw as an affront to God. Warren's relationship with Amanda Cobb ended when she noticed that there were nubs growing from the bruises on his back. Not wanting to explain what he thought was happening, Warreb abruptly broke up with her. Jilted, Amanda then started dating Brandon Hardy. Fearing what may be happening to him, Warren began studying on birds and their molting patterns. On the night of the annual Hell Night, Warren came to aid Andrew, who was being hazed by his classmates for being a freshman. Warren knocked out Brandon and rushed Andrew to his room. There, a clearly smitten Andrew, revealed that he knew Warren's secret. Warren was later surprised when he discovered that the grows were wings that were starting to grow from his back. Warren later came to the aid of another bullied student, Cameron Hodge who began to idolize Warren. As Warren's wings began to grow in size, they became hard to conceal, and he started strapping them to his back. In order to avoid suspicion, he abruptly quit all athletics in school, much to the confusion of his coaches and administrators. When a fire broke out in his dorm at Phillips Academy in Exeter, New Hampshire, Warren decided to do something about it. Using costumes from the theater storeroom, Warren dressed up as an Angel and saved those imperiled by the fire. One of these students was Cameron Hodge, who instantly recognized Warren despite his disguise, although he kept this secret for many decades afterward. During the Christmas break, Andrew convinced Warren to stay behind instead of going home for the holidays. Warren took the opportunity to test out his new wings and their ability to make him fly. There was a near accident when he accidentally dropped Andrew in a frozen pond, but was able to revive him with CPR. It was not long after this that Warren discovered that the school priest, Father Reynolds, was secretly molesting Andrew, and Warren decided to do something about it. Using the props from the theater department again, Warren disguised himself as Michael the Archangel and tricked Father Reynolds into confessing his crimes. As Reynolds was being led away, Brandon Hardy teased Andrew, and Warren once again came to his defense. This led to a brawl that included Amanda Cobb
fields.personality: Angel used to be involved in a long love triangle with Cyclops over Jean Grey when they were teenagers. Wanda briefly dated Angel. During his time-displacement, Angel dated Laura Kinney. They apparently broke up off-panel before Warren returned to the past. Angel formerly dated Candy Southern who was later killed by Cameron Hodge. Angel was in a long-term relationship with Psylocke, but they eventually broke up when Betsy showed feelings for Neal Shaara. Angel reignited his relationship with Psylocke, partly due to the fact that she was helping to control his transformations into Archangel, but they once again broke up after Angel lost his memory after being resurrected. Angel also used to date Husk.
equipment: Image Inducer
transportation: formerly X-Men Stratojet, X-Copter, Professor Xavier's Rolls Royce, Sentinel Air Transport, Champjet, X-Factor Plane, and various aircrafts constructed by Ship.
weapons: Wing blades
fields.notes: He is possibly a representative of the subspecies known as the Cheyarafim, having wings and Neyaphem-burning blood, but Azazel refuted this allegation, on the basis that Warren was a recent mutant, stating that his power set was a mere coincidence, although Azazel was curious about Warren's lineage. After being stabbed with the Celestial Life Seed, both his Archangel and Warren Worthington personas were destroyed. The seed used Archangel as "soil" to grow a new person, resulting in the new Angel.
fields.trivia: Angel was a member of the Hellfire Club, a position he inherited from his father, though he doesn't often officially associate with them, and is not a member of the Inner Circle. Warren can selectively bring out different aspects of his Archangel form, such as just forming his metallic wings in use for defense. Angel has once impersonated the Angel Michael, and has been compared to the Angel Raphael. Warren did not have a particularly high opinion of his teammate Cyclops. He considered Cyclops a boor, who "couldn't convince a drowning man to take a life preserver". Namor has remarked that Warren stands out for his arrogance. Warren has used the email address 'wworthington@xmen.cerebo.x' At one point Warren's parents lived at 4739 Anderson Lane, Fort Washington, New York, 10016. The real world zip code for this address actually matches Midtown, Manhattan.
fields.species: Mutant (purportedly Cheyarafim throwback); later granted Techno-Organic wings by Apocalypse on his Celestial Ship, then reborn from the Celestial Seed

warren worthington iii clone.name: Warren Worthington III (Clone)
warren worthington iii clone.origin: In hopes to get rid of his Archangel powers, Warren Worthington III contacted the Clan Akkaba. They cut off his "tainted" wings and secretly used them to create an army of Archangels called the Death-Flight. One of those clones escaped and was found by Magneto; however, the Archangel was little more than a mindless drone, so Magneto contacted Psylocke and convinced her to help whom he mistakenly believed to be the real Warren Worthington. Psylocke tried many times to reach Warren's consciousness, but all attempts were futile. In the end, under her psychic leash Archangel became simply a heavy hitter in Magneto's X-Men. After dealing with the Dark Riders, Psylocke tried to scan Warren's mind one more time, when suddenly she was taken into Warren's psyche represented by a city in ruins, with a piece of Warren inside. Warren's consciousness warned her that the city of Green Ridge would be ravaged by an army of Archangels unless the X-Men stopped him. Psylocke and Magneto went to investigate, and found the real Angel there. They soon came to know of Angel's deal with Clan Akkaba. Clan Akkaba revealed their true intentions in helping Warren, when their army of cloned Archangels led by the escaped clone attacked Green Ridge. Psylocke tried to control him once again, but failed. In the end, Angel, realizing that Archangel needed his humanity, merged with the last remaining clone, the one who had become a part of Magneto's X-Men, creating a new being. This new Archangel was unsure of who or what he now was, but was determined to find out. He swore off all violence and returned with Magneto's X-Men to their base in the Savage Land.

warren worthington jr.name: Warren Worthington Jr.
warren worthington jr.origin: ===Early Life=== Warren Worthington Jr. was born into wealth and privilege as the son of industrialist Warren Worthington, Sr. , the head of Worthington Industries, a company long held by the family. He had an elder brother, Burt Worthington, who became the family's black sheep after pursuing a life of crime. Warren Jr. , in contrast, followed in his father's footsteps and eventually rose to the position of CEO of Worthington Industries. Warren met and married New York socialite Kathryn Worthington, and together they had a son, Warren Worthington III. ===Hellfire Club=== thumb|left|250px|The Hellfire Club. As a leading businessman, Warren Jr. moved in the same circles as other wealthy elites such as Howard Stark, John Braddock, and Sebastian Shaw. He was invited to join the exclusive Hellfire Club, where he regularly attended social gatherings, though he never attained a seat within the Inner Circle. On one occasion, he brought his son to a party at the Club while Logan, then a covert operative, infiltrated the mansion to steal files. Warren Jr. was unaware of the intrusion. During another visit, Warren introduced his son to Shinobi Shaw, hoping to foster a bond between the heirs of the Worthington and Shaw families, though the two boys soon drifted apart. ===Mutant Son=== Warren Jr. grew increasingly frustrated with his son, who preferred solitude to the social life his father encouraged. He scolded the boy for isolating himself, even on birthdays. He frequently found Warren III climbing onto the roof or into trees, and once his son narrowly avoided injury when he fell, landing only by chance in the family's newly renovated pool. Concerned, his parents decided to send him away to private school. In adolescence, Warren III began experiencing painful growths on his back that eventually developed into wings. His parents noticed the changes, though their response was one of embarrassment and emotional distance. They expressed hopes that someone might "cure" him. Warren Jr. enrolled his son at St. Joseph's Preparatory School, where the boy remained apart from them except during holidays. When his son called one Christmas to say he would not be coming home, Warren coldly replied that he had already sent money, the same as the year before, before leaving for a party. Even at their son's graduation, he and Kathryn attended with indifference. ===Xavier's School for Gifted Youngsters=== When Professor Charles Xavier invited Warren III to join his school for mutants, Warren Jr. and Kathryn accepted, hoping a cure could be found for their son's mutation. During this time, they asked their son to help locate his missing aunt Miriam Worthington, who had vanished in Brazil. They later welcomed their son home for dinner but were stunned when he left abruptly after being summoned to battle the Sentinels. During another visit to the Xavier Institute, the Worthingtons encountered Magneto, who briefly placed them in a trance until the X-Men drove him off. Xavier subsequently erased their memories of the incident. ===Brother's Return=== Warren Jr.'s brother Burt Worthington became involved in diamond smuggling. After being released from prison, Burt posed as reformed and re-entered his brother’s life, secretly using Worthington Industries to mask his smuggling operations. When Warren Jr. discovered the truth, he threatened to expose him. Burt later returned as the criminal known as the "Dazzler". While Warren Jr. was in declining health, Burt's agents murdered him during an attack that also targeted Warren III, who was away on a date. Dazzler subsequently kidnapped Warren III and his girlfriend Candy Southern, forcing Angel to steal the world's largest diamond for his spatial destructor device. Angel foiled the plot by substituting the jewel with a glass replica, causing the device to self-destruct and seemingly killing his uncle. ===Brother's Revenge=== Burt survived his apparent death and resurfaced with an elaborate scheme to usurp his brother's fortune. Adopting a more insidious approach than before, Burt sought to manipulate and ultimately seduce Kathryn, intending to secure the Worthington wealth through her. While posing as reformed, he ingratiated himself into Kathryn's life with the assistance of his accomplice, Doctor Stuart, who provided medical cover for Burt's schemes. Angel and the X-Men soon uncovered Burt's deception and attempted to intervene, but not before tragedy struck. Burt poisoned Kathryn, leading to her sudden death, and confronted Warren III in a bitter clash that reopened old family wounds. Despite Burt's attempt to escape justice, the X-Men subdued him and handed both him and Doctor Stuart over to the authorities.

warrior zero.name: Warrior Zero
warrior zero.origin: Warrior One was the best soldier in all of Prime. When Silver Surfer and Dawn Greenwood visited Prime to have the best ice cream in the universe, he accidentally caused Banker One to panic and call the army for help. Their response was Warrior One, who blindly fought the Silver Surfer even though he tried to prevent a conflict. After removing his mastery badge from him, the Warrior One was no longer so, and was ordered by the new Warrior One, the former Warrior Two, to stop the fight. As he was now an outcast, the former Warrior One proclaimed himself "Warrior Zero," and vowed revenge on the Surfer. thumb|left|With badge, as Warrior One After long having scoured the cosmos to find his enemy, Warrior Zero confronted the Silver Surfer and Dawn Greenwood in Apinaxis Major. Due to an event they urgently had to attend to, the Surfer flew away in spite of Warrior Zero's challenge. Warrior Zero caught up with them and surrounded himself and the Surfer in a trans-warp bubble, which was to remain sealed until a victor was declared. The Surfer accepted the challenge, and let Warrior Zero win only to get rid of him. Warrior Zero confronted the Surfer for a third time after discovering he had simply faked his death. Fed up with Warrior Zero's impertinence, the Surfer swiftly knocked him out with a single blow, and forced Warrior Zero to renounce his crusade. While left stranded in space, Warrior Zero declared he was no longer fit to be a warrior, and was instead to be Zero.

fields.history: Warrior One was the best soldier in all of Prime. When Silver Surfer and Dawn Greenwood visited Prime to have the best ice cream in the universe, he accidentally caused Banker One to panic and call the army for help. Their response was Warrior One, who blindly fought the Silver Surfer even though he tried to prevent a conflict. After removing his mastery badge from him, the Warrior One was no longer so, and was ordered by the new Warrior One, the former Warrior Two, to stop the fight. As he was now an outcast, the former Warrior One proclaimed himself "Warrior Zero," and vowed revenge on the Surfer. thumb|left|With badge, as Warrior One After long having scoured the cosmos to find his enemy, Warrior Zero confronted the Silver Surfer and Dawn Greenwood in Apinaxis Major. Due to an event they urgently had to attend to, the Surfer flew away in spite of Warrior Zero's challenge. Warrior Zero caught up with them and surrounded himself and the Surfer in a trans-warp bubble, which was to remain sealed until a victor was declared. The Surfer accepted the challenge, and let Warrior Zero win only to get rid of him. Warrior Zero confronted the Surfer for a third time after discovering he had simply faked his death. Fed up with Warrior Zero's impertinence, the Surfer swiftly knocked him out with a single blow, and forced Warrior Zero to renounce his crusade. While left stranded in space, Warrior Zero declared he was no longer fit to be a warrior, and was instead to be Zero.

warshot.name: Warshot
warshot.origin: Warshot was a Kree weapons master who was exiled from Hala for illegally providing weapons to a rebellion. He was eventually found by the Shi'ar Empire and hired for a position on their black ops team, the Death Commandos. For their first assignment, they were sent to Earth where he participated in the extermination of the Grey Genome. However, they failed to kill Rachel Summers and were forced to retreat back to Chandilar. They later loyally served under Araki during a civil war that broke out across the entire Shi'ar Empire. The Death Commandos were next tasked by Oracle with killing Deathbird and anyone with her. Warshot and the new Black Cloak stayed on their ship to monitor the heatrates and give orders while the other Death Commandos boarded Deathbird's escort shuttle. Eventually, all of the Death Commandos were either killed or defeated, so as a last ditch effort, Black Cloak told Warshot to destroy the shuttle. This also killed the rest of team, but they were able to capture Cannonball, Cypher, Sunspot, Smasher, and Deathbird. However, before Black Cloak could kill Deathbird, Sunspot got in the way and Deathbird was able to escape. After being unable to find her, Black Cloak started torturing the remaining captives but Deathbird returned and stabbed Warshot from behind before decapitating Black Cloak.

warwolf cybertek.name: Warwolf (Cybertek)
warwolf cybertek.origin: Warwolf was a prototype-stage cyborg development built as a hunter-seeker, assassination device by Cybertek Systems, Inc, the applied cybernetics division of Roxxon Oil, and stored in Roxxon Branch Warehouse #23, Lynchburg, Virginia. A melding of a wolf's brain with a computer, it was created by Cybertek head Harlan Ryker before Ryker oversaw a later project, the creation of the human cyborg Deathlok. Cybertek scientist William Hansen contributed to the design of the cyborg, and was familiar with its capacities. Cybertek programmer Jim Dworman knew about Warwolf, including several details of it. When Cybertek's illegal activities were discovered, many Cybertek staff members were arrested and sent to the Danbury Maximum Security Federal Penitentiary, with the NSA in charge of the investigation. A number of them agreed to testify against Ryker, adding to the evidence that the NSA had copied from Cybertek's computers in their Paterson, New Jersey HQ. Ryker used his sole phone call to activate Warwolf and command it to destroy the stored evidence, both the copies in the NSA facilities in Washington, D.C. and the originals in Paterson, and to murder the witnesses. Warwolf first attacked the NSA offices, then moved to Newark, New Jersey, to murder Hansen, who was on probation after making a deal. Warwolf attacked Hansen while the later was driving through the highway and caused a car crash. Warwolf then went to Cybertek's lab, by then closed for good except for the presence of Dworman, who oversaw the closure, and of Dworman's friend Michael Collins, whom Ryker had turned into the cyborg Deathlok. Deathlok was trying to obtain information relevant to his current state in Cybertek's computer. Warwolf attacked the facilities and destroyed the files, even though Deathlok opposed him. Both Warwolf and Deathlok escaped before NSA Agents Able and Baker arrived, vainly hoping to find a new copy of the computer records there - the NSA explained that Ryker's case was substantiated by eyewitnesses. Understanding Warwolf's goals, Deathlok tracked the locations of the witnesses, and foresaw that Warwolf would attack the Danbury prison; through Dworman, he warned the NSA about the prisoners' security, but the NSA thought the prison would provide enough security. Deathlok, wanting to confront Warwolf, travelled there on a helicopter. Warwolf attacked the prison, activating the alarms, and targeted Cybertek accountant John Rozum's cell, but Deathlok rushed onto him and took him to the prison's open courtyard. Deathlok irreparably damaged the cyborg on a fall and, knowing through his sensors that the wolf brain would die in six hours, Deathlok executed Warwolf. Afterward, Dworman accessed Warwolf's backup memory and obtained proof that Ryker had ordered Warwolf to murder Hansen, thus providing evidence against Ryker.

warzone mercenary.name: Warzone (Mercenary)
warzone mercenary.origin: Warzone was ordered by the Leader to kill his ex-leader: the Foreigner. He joined with Battlescar and Dead Aim, and they waited for the Foreigner near Dead-Aim's base. Warzone attacked the Foreigner, but his energy blast missed his ex-leader and destroyed a car. He had no time to renew the attack because Spider-Man hit him from behind. Warzone, not injured but only vexed by Spider-Man's loquacity, tried to blast him but missed, only smashing the ground. Soon after Warzone was shocked to understand that the satellite was falling just on heads, and he could only watch as Spider-Man saved the day. Warzone was knocked out by the explosion. Later, Warzone was arrested by the Police together with his colleagues.

washington jones.name: Washington Jones
washington jones.origin: Washington "Wash" Jones was an affluent African-American who lived in New York City during World War II and joined Captain America's Sentinels of Liberty youth group. He met Captain America's sidekick Bucky and became part of the Young Allies, a group of wartime youths who worked to fight Nazi spies and other menaces during World War II. ===Preface: Truth and Fiction=== It has been revealed that a lot of the Young Allies wartime adventures were made into a comic book as propaganda for the United States to earn support in the war effort, especially among young impressionable people. The comic book, while based on true events where often times embellished, and sensationalized. Further, to "protect" the identities of the Young Allies (however, in later years, Bucky would suspect it was to avoid having to pay out royalties for the use of their likenesses) were all portrayed as caricatures of themselves, and were all portrayed as being young adolescents around the age of 12 while in real life they were in their late teens to early adulthood and eventually became old enough to enlist in the military and see action in the battle field. The least flattering portrayal of any of the Young Allies was the character based on Washington. Renamed "Whitewash Jones" the character was a dimwitted, racial stereotype that was modeled after a minstrel show. While considered socially acceptable at the time of their publication, Washington's portrayal would be considered greatly offensive by today's standards. At the time of their publication, Washington considered his portrayal as ridiculous. Although he would note that he had been treated worse when off duty, he remarked that "You could tell that those writers have never been up town". The fictional accounts of the Young Allies are the most complete record of their activities during World War II, however how much of these tales are fiction and how much are truth have yet to be completely chronicled. For the purposes of clarity between what is known to be fully factual and what is regarded as sensationalized fiction, both will be addressed separately in this profile. ===Real Life History=== Shortly after the formation of the Young Allies, Wash joined his comrades in smashing a Nazi spy ring in New York leading to a clash with the Red Skull. The youths were assisted by the timely arrival of Captain America and the Human Torch. left|thumb|Washington Carver during World War 2 In 1943, Patrick and the Young Allies were sent to Hollywood, California for a war bond drive. The rally was soon marred by a panic caused by Bucky and Toro's foe Lady Lotus, and they soon broke up the disruption. Patrick and his friends were then ordered by the military to report to Democracy Pictures to participate in a film in support of the war. They were once more targeted by Lady Lotus who hypnotized actors to attack them, and then took Toro under her control. Capturing the team, Lady Lotus hypnotized the rest of the group and as part of her plan to take over the American west coast sent the group in a B-17 and P-40 to attack Muroc Army Airfield. However, Washington Jones snapped out of Lady Lotus' control and managed to help the others break free from her mind control. They would get the air fields participation in a ruse that made it appear their attack was a success. Pretending to still be under the control of Lady Lotus, the Young Allies got close enough to attack her. During the battle, Toro managed to knock a crystal that Lotus was using to boost her powers and it was subsequently swallowed up in the Earth. Lady Lotus then fled, vowing to get revenge against the Young Allies someday. Coming of age, Washington became a member of the United States Air Force and saw action during the liberation of France. In 1944, Washington reunited with his fellow Young Allies during their downtime. Meeting in France, the Young Allies had their festivities cut short when Geoff spotted German operative Hauptmann Kleinschmidt. Washington would rode his motorcycle into battle. When Kleinschmidt attempted to flee in a truck, Wash sped after him, allowing Bucky to jump on board and force the German to crash. This was the last time the Young Allies fought together, but they all stayed in touch over the years. ===Fictional History=== thumb|left|"Whitewash" Jones Circa 1941 (This ridiculous stereotype was socially acceptable prior to the Civil Rights movement, however is considered highly offensive by today's standards) For a detailed account of the fictional history of Whitewash Jones see the Fictional History of the Young Allies. ===After the War=== After the war, Washington rejoined the Air Force following President Truman's desegregation of the Armed Forces. He served the Air Force with pride during the Korean War. By the time he retired from service, he had earned the rank of Colonel. Further, to "protect" the identities of the Young Allies (however, in later years, Bucky would suspect it was to avoid having to pay out royalties for the use of their likenesses) were all portrayed as caricatures of themselves, and were all portrayed as being young adolescents around the age of 12 while in real life they were in their late teens to early adulthood and eventually became old enough to enlist in the military and see action in the battle field. The least flattering portrayal of any of the Young Allies was the character based on Washington. Renamed "Whitewash Jones" the character was a dimwitted, racial stereotype that was modeled after a minstrel show. While considered socially acceptable at the time of their publication, Washington's portrayal would be considered greatly offensive by today's standards. At the time of their publication, Washington considered his portrayal as ridiculous. Although he would note that he had been treated worse when off duty, he remarked that "You could tell that those writers have never been up town". The fictional accounts of the Young Allies are the most complete record of their activities during World War II, however how much of these tales are fiction and how much are truth have yet to be completely chronicled. For the purposes of clarity between what is known to be fully factual and what is regarded as sensationalized fiction, both will be addressed separately in this profile. ===Real Life History=== Shortly after the formation of the Young Allies, Wash joined his comrades in smashing a Nazi spy ring in New York leading to a clash with the Red Skull. The youths were assisted by the timely arrival of Captain America and the Human Torch. left|thumb|Washington Carver during World War 2 In 1943, Patrick and the Young Allies were sent to Hollywood, California for a war bond drive. The rally was soon marred by a panic caused by Bucky and Toro's foe Lady Lotus, and they soon broke up the disruption. Patrick and his friends were then ordered by the military to report to Democracy Pictures to participate in a film in support of the war. They were once more targeted by Lady Lotus who hypnotized actors to attack them, and then took Toro under her control. Capturing the team, Lady Lotus hypnotized the rest of the group and as part of her plan to take over the American west coast sent the group in a B-17 and P-40 to attack Muroc Army Airfield. However, Washington Jones snapped out of Lady Lotus' control and managed to help the others break free from her mind control. They would get the air fields participation in a ruse that made it appear their attack was a success. Pretending to still be under the control of Lady Lotus, the Young Allies got close enough to attack her. During the battle, Toro managed to knock a crystal that Lotus was using to boost her powers and it was subsequently swallowed up in the Earth. Lady Lotus then fled, vowing to get revenge against the Young Allies someday. Coming of age, Washington became a member of the United States Air Force and saw action during the liberation of France. In 1944, Washington reunited with his fellow Young Allies during their downtime. Meeting in France, the Young Allies had their festivities cut short when Geoff spotted German operative Hauptmann Kleinschmidt. Washington would rode his motorcycle into battle. When Kleinschmidt attempted to flee in a truck, Wash sped after him, allowing Bucky to jump on board and force the German to crash. This was the last time the Young Allies fought together, but they all stayed in touch over the years. ===Fictional History=== thumb|left|"Whitewash" Jones Circa 1941 (This ridiculous stereotype was socially acceptable prior to the Civil Rights movement, however is considered highly offensive by today's standards) For a detailed account of the fictional history of Whitewash Jones see the Fictional History of the Young Allies. ===After the War=== After the war, Washington rejoined the Air Force following President Truman's desegregation of the Armed Forces. waste von kampf.origin: A Nazi spy undervoer as a British officer during WW2. When time-travellers from the future, including J. Jonah Jackal, were arrested and accused of being spies on a manned rocket, von Kampf decided to act because he knew that the Nazis had failed to develop manned rockets - so he wanted Jackal and his crew to fly the rocket back to Germany where it'd be reverse-engineered. Jackal recognized von Kampf as a Nazi spy, because Jackal had seen von Kampf's photo in a history book. Jackal was rescued by another time-traveller, Spider-Ham, who knocked down von Kampf and hung him from the Big Ben before restoring the time machine and going back home.

fields.notes: This character's name is a joke: Kampf is German for "fight", famously used in Adolf Hitler's book title "Mein Kampf" ("my fight"), and the particle "von" for surnames can be translated as "of". "Waste" is not a German word, meaning "garbage" or "misuse". Thus, his name is "a waste of fight."
